definition_zh: 食虫动物；以昆虫为主食的动物（也指食虫植物）
definition_en: an animal or plant that feeds chiefly on insects
core_image: 一只小兽扒开朽木，专挑里面的虫子吃
scene: A shrew is a true insectivore that hunts beetles and grubs in the leaf litter.
sceneCN: 这里 insectivore 是「食虫动物」（第 1 个义项：以昆虫为主食的动物）；句意：鼩鼱是真正的食虫动物，在落叶层中捕食甲虫和蛴螬。

pos.zh: 食虫动物；食虫生物；食虫植物（可数，复数 insectivores）

senses.title: An animal that lives on insects
senses.definition: an animal whose diet consists mainly of insects
senses.definitionCN: 以昆虫为主要食物的动物
senses.example: Shrews and moles are insectivores that seldom surface above the litter.
senses.exampleCN: 鼩鼱和鼹鼠是食虫动物，很少爬到落叶层以上活动。
senses.why: The word joins Latin for insect with a Latin root meaning to devour, so it names a feeder purely by what it eats.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把拉丁语的「昆虫」与表示「吞食」的词根连在一起，完全按「吃什么」来给取食者命名。

senses.title: A member of an old mammal order
senses.definition: a mammal formerly placed in the order Insectivora, such as a shrew, a mole or a hedgehog
senses.definitionCN: 曾被归入食虫目的哺乳动物，如鼩鼱、鼹鼠或刺猬
senses.example: The hedgehog was long treated as a typical insectivore by taxonomists.
senses.exampleCN: 刺猬长期被分类学家当作典型的食虫目动物。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century zoology needed a label for mammals grouped by an insect diet, and it simply reused the everyday word as an order name.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪的动物学需要给「按食虫习性归为一类」的哺乳动物一个名称，于是直接把这个日常词升格为目名。

senses.title: A plant that traps insects
senses.definition: a plant that captures and digests insects to obtain nutrients
senses.definitionCN: 捕捉并消化昆虫以获取养分的植物
senses.example: The sundew is an insectivore that supplements poor soil with trapped midges.
senses.exampleCN: 茅膏菜是一种食虫植物，用捕获的蠓虫弥补贫瘠土壤的养分。
senses.why: Botany extended the eater-and-food relation to plants, keeping the insect as the food and the plant as the consumer.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把「吃与被吃」的关系套用到植物身上，昆虫仍是食物，植物成了取食一方。

senses.title: Any predator of insects
senses.definition: broadly, any bird, reptile, amphibian or fish whose prey is largely insects
senses.definitionCN: 泛指以昆虫为主要猎物的鸟类、爬行类、两栖类或鱼类
senses.example: Many songbirds are insectivores during the breeding season.
senses.exampleCN: 许多鸣禽在繁殖季都是食虫动物。
senses.why: Once the label means insect-eater, it can describe any predator whose prey is mostly insects, not only the mammals of the old order.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词的意思是「吃昆虫的」，它就能描述任何以昆虫为主的捕食者，而不限于旧目里的哺乳动物。

senses.title: A role in the food web
senses.definition: an organism assigned to the insect-eating functional group in community ecology
senses.definitionCN: 群落生态学中归入「食虫」功能群的生物
senses.example: The study compared insectivores and granivores across the same grassland.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究在同一片草地上比较了食虫动物与食种子动物。
senses.why: Ecology classifies organisms by what they do rather than what they are, so the old dietary noun became the name of a functional guild.
senses.whyCN: 生态学按「做什么」而不是「是什么」来分类，于是这个古老的「食性名词」变成了功能群的名称。

senses.title: A person who eats insects
senses.definition: a person whose diet regularly includes insects, especially in entomophagy research
senses.definitionCN: 日常饮食中包含昆虫的人，常见于食虫研究语境
senses.example: The survey asked whether local insectivores preferred roasted or boiled larvae.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查询问当地的食虫者更喜欢烤的还是煮的幼虫。
senses.why: The same eater-and-food pattern applies to humans, though the word is far rarer here than the dietary term entomophagy.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「吃与被吃」模式也适用于人，不过在这个意义上，这个词远不如表示「食虫」的 entomophagy 常用。

senses.title: A natural pest controller
senses.definition: an insect-eating species valued in agriculture for suppressing pests
senses.definitionCN: 在农业上因抑制害虫而受重视的食虫物种
senses.example: Farmers installed bat boxes because the insectivores cut moth numbers sharply.
senses.exampleCN: 农民挂起蝙蝠箱，因为这些食虫动物大幅减少了蛾的数量。
senses.why: Conservation writing shifts from what the animal eats to what that eating does for people, turning the eater into a service provider.
senses.whyCN: 保护类写作把重点从「它吃什么」转到「这种吃对人有什么用」，于是取食者变成了服务的提供者。

senses.title: An insect-eater in the fossil record
senses.definition: a fossil species reconstructed as insect-eating from its teeth or gut contents
senses.definitionCN: 依据牙齿或胃肠内容物推断为食虫的化石物种
senses.example: Paleontologists identified the tiny jaw as an insectivore from its sharp molars.
senses.exampleCN: 古生物学家根据其锋利的臼齿，把这枚小颌骨鉴定为食虫类。
senses.why: Paleontology infers diet from anatomy, so the same word marks a reconstructed feeding habit rather than an observed one.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学依据解剖结构推断食性，因此这个词标记的是重建出来的取食习惯，而不是直接观察到的行为。

intro.en: Insectivore is a scientific compound of a Latin noun for insect and a Latin root meaning to devour.
intro.cn: insectivore 是一个科学复合词，由拉丁语「昆虫」名词与表示「吞食」的拉丁词根构成。

items.en: Insect goes back to Latin insectum, literally 'a thing cut into', from insecare (in- 'into' + secare 'to cut'). It was a loan-translation of Greek entomon, which also meant 'cut in two'.
items.cn: insect 上溯至拉丁语 insectum，字面是「被切开的东西」，来自 insecare（in-「进入」+ secare「切」）。它是对希腊语 entomon 的仿译，而 entomon 同样有「切成两段」之意。

items.en: The second element comes from Latin vorare, 'to devour, swallow whole', the source of voracious and of the -vore ending in carnivore and herbivore.
items.cn: 第二个成分来自拉丁语 vorare「吞食、整口吞下」，也是 voracious 以及 carnivore、herbivore 中 -vore 词尾的来源。

items.en: French insectivore and scientific Latin Insectivora brought the two elements together in the early nineteenth century. The connecting -i- belongs to the Latin stem, not to English word formation.
items.cn: 法语 insectivore 与科学拉丁语 Insectivora 在 19 世纪初把两个成分组合起来。连接元音 -i- 来自拉丁词干，而不是英语自身的构词习惯。

items.en: Insectivora was a mammalian order covering shrews, moles and hedgehogs. Molecular studies showed the group was not a single lineage, so the order has been abandoned, though the everyday word survives.
items.cn: Insectivora 曾是一个哺乳动物目，包含鼩鼱、鼹鼠与刺猬。分子研究显示这一群体并非单一谱系，因此该目已被废弃，但日常用词仍然保留。

items.en: From the mid-nineteenth century the word also named insect-catching plants; Darwin's book on insectivorous plants in 1875 fixed the usage in English.
items.cn: 自 19 世纪中叶起，这个词也用来指捕虫植物；达尔文 1875 年关于食虫植物的著作使这一用法在英语中固定下来。

note.en: The first group holds words built from the same elements; the second holds words for other feeding types.
note.cn: 第一组是用相同构词成分造出的词；第二组是表示其他食性的词。

entries.definition: Describes an animal or plant with that diet; insectivore is the creature itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述具有这种食性的动物或植物；insectivore 指生物本身。

entries.definition: Names the habit or diet itself, so it cannot stand for a shrew or a sundew.
entries.definitionCN: 指食虫的习性饮食本身，不能用来指鼩鼱或茅膏菜这类生物。

entries.definition: The prey; it carries no information about who eats it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被捕食的昆虫，本身不包含「谁来吃」的信息。

entries.definition: An animal that feeds on detritus, the dead and decaying fragments of organisms; the food differs, the eating pattern matches.
entries.definitionCN: 指以腐屑为食的动物，腐屑是生物死亡后破碎的残余；食物不同，但取食模式相同。

entries.definition: An animal that eats other animals, insects included; insectivore is the narrower, diet-specific term.
entries.definitionCN: 指吃其他动物的动物，昆虫也在其中；insectivore 范围更窄，专指食虫。

entries.definition: An animal that eats both plant and animal matter; an insectivore may take the occasional plant, but insects dominate.
entries.definitionCN: 指动植物都吃的动物；食虫动物偶尔也吃植物，但以昆虫为主。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real relatives and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: insect + -vore 'devourer': an insect-devourer.
normal.cn: insect「昆虫」+ -vore「吞食者」：吞食昆虫者。

normal.en: The family runs insectivore, insectivorous, insectivory and insect.
normal.cn: 同族词有 insectivore、insectivorous、insectivory、insect。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the technical senses: obligate insectivore, insectivore guild, insectivore species.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义项：专性食虫动物、食虫功能群、食虫物种。

normal.en: A shrew in the leaf litter is the picture the word was made for.
normal.cn: 落叶层里的鼩鼱，就是这个词最初描绘的画面。

normal.en: The -vore ending recurs in carnivore, herbivore and omnivore, all naming eaters.
normal.cn: -vore 词尾在 carnivore、herbivore、omnivore 中反复出现，都表示「吃某物者」。

abstract.en: Picture a menu with only one item: insects. Whoever lives on that menu is an insectivore.
abstract.cn: 想象一份只有一道菜的菜单：昆虫。靠这份菜单过活的，就是食虫动物。

abstract.en: Think of a pest-control worker paid in protein instead of money.
abstract.cn: 把它想成一个用蛋白质而不是工资结算的害虫防治工。

abstract.en: A pitfall trap in the soil is the animal's pantry: whatever falls in is dinner.
abstract.cn: 土壤里的陷阱是这种动物的食品柜：掉进去什么，晚餐就是什么。

examples.en: Shrews are insectivores that must eat almost constantly to fuel their fast metabolism.
examples.cn: 鼩鼱是食虫动物，必须几乎不停地进食来支撑快速代谢。

examples.en: The fossil jaw suggests an insectivore about the size of a thumb.
examples.cn: 这块化石颌骨显示出一种只有拇指大小的食虫动物。

examples.en: Conservationists count insectivores among the best natural controls of crop pests.
examples.cn: 保护工作者把食虫动物列为农作物害虫最好的天然控制者之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（在……里）+ sect（切）+ vore（吞）→ 把虫子切开吞下去 → 食虫动物

root: 拉丁语 insectum「昆虫」（由 insecare「切开」而来，in- + secare「切」）+ 拉丁语 vorare「吞食」+ 名词后缀 -ore → insectivore，字面即「吞食昆虫者」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one relation: an eater and its insect food. Classification, botany, ecology, agriculture, human diet and paleontology each borrowed the word for their own version of that relation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一个关系生长出来：取食者与它的昆虫食物。分类学、植物学、生态学、农业、人类饮食与古生物学各自借用了这个词，来描述自己版本的那层关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small hunter whose entire menu is insects.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个整份菜单只有昆虫的小型捕食者。

chain: A ROLE IN THE FOOD WEB

branches.en: THE CORE: a diet of insects defines the animal, and taxonomy once borrowed that definition as an order name.
branches.cn: 核心：昆虫食性定义了这类动物，分类学曾把这一界定借去当作目名。

branches.en: OTHER EATERS: plants and non-mammalian predators join the category whenever insects are their main food.
branches.cn: 其他取食者：只要昆虫是主要食物，植物和非哺乳类捕食者也能进入这一类别。

branches.en: THE ROLE: ecology ignores species and groups anything that eats insects into one functional guild.
branches.cn: 角色：生态学不看物种，只把所有吃昆虫的生物归入同一个功能群。

branches.en: THE HUMAN: people who eat insects are described by the same pattern, though a different technical term is usual.
branches.cn: 人类：吃昆虫的人也能套用同一模式，只是通常使用另一个专业术语。

branches.en: APPLIED VIEWS: agriculture sees a pest controller, paleontology sees a diet reconstructed from teeth.
branches.cn: 应用视角：农业看到的是害虫控制者，古生物学看到的是从牙齿重建出来的食性。

intro.en: Insectivore is a two-part scientific compound whose meaning is transparent from its Latin pieces.
intro.cn: insectivore 是一个两部分组成的科学复合词，其含义从拉丁语成分看一目了然。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Latin: insectum for the prey and vorare for eating. The linking -i- is the stem vowel of insectum, and -ore marks the agent.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都来自拉丁语：insectum 指猎物，vorare 指吞食。连接元音 -i- 是 insectum 的词干元音，-ore 标记施动者。

items.example: The hedgehog is a familiar insectivore of gardens.
items.exampleCN: 刺猬是花园里常见的食虫动物。

items.example: The insectivorous bird catches moths on the wing.
items.exampleCN: 这种食虫鸟在空中捕捉飞蛾。

items.example: Insectivory evolved independently in several mammal groups.
items.exampleCN: 食虫习性在多个哺乳动物类群中独立演化。

items.meaningCN: 六足的小型无脊椎动物
items.example: The bird searched the bark for insects.
items.exampleCN: 这只鸟在树皮上搜寻昆虫。

items.example: The orchard reduced insecticide use after planting hedgerows.
items.exampleCN: 果园在种下树篱后减少了杀虫剂的使用。

items.meaning: eating greedily and in large amounts
items.example: The larvae are voracious consumers of leaves.
items.exampleCN: 这些幼虫是叶子的贪婪取食者。

items.example: A carnivore of this size needs large prey.
items.exampleCN: 这个体型的食肉动物需要大型猎物。

items.example: The herbivore grazes between the shrubs.
items.exampleCN: 这种食草动物在灌木之间觅食。

latinEntries.meaning: an insect; literally 'a thing cut into'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 昆虫；字面为「被切开的东西」

core_image: 一片叶子合拢，把落脚的苍蝇裹进消化液
scene: The sundew is an insectivorous plant that digests flies on its sticky leaves.
sceneCN: 这里 insectivorous 是「食虫的」（第 2 个义项：植物捕食并消化昆虫）；句意：茅膏菜是食虫植物，用黏性叶片消化苍蝇。

pos.zh: 食虫的；以昆虫为食的；（旧分类）食虫目的

senses.title: Living on insects
senses.definition: describing an animal whose diet is made up mostly of insects
senses.definitionCN: 描述以昆虫为主要食物的动物
senses.example: Insectivorous bats emerge at dusk to hunt moths over the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 食虫蝙蝠在黄昏时飞出，在果园上方捕食飞蛾。
senses.why: The suffix -ous turns the noun insectivore into a description, so the diet becomes a property of the animal.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ous 把名词 insectivore 变成描述性形容词，于是食性成了动物的一种属性。

senses.title: Plants that catch and digest
senses.definition: describing a plant that traps insects and absorbs nutrients from them
senses.definitionCN: 描述捕捉昆虫并从中吸收养分的植物
senses.example: Insectivorous leaves often lose their trapping colour in shady conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 食虫植物的叶片在遮阴条件下常会失去捕虫的颜色。
senses.why: Botany applies the human-scale eater to a plant, and the adjective lets the plant modify leaf, species or habitat.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把「取食者」这一人间尺度套用到植物，形容词形式便于直接修饰 leaf、species 或 habitat。

senses.title: Of the old order Insectivora
senses.definition: in older taxonomy, belonging to the mammalian order Insectivora
senses.definitionCN: 旧分类学中属于哺乳动物食虫目的
senses.example: The insectivorous families were later split across several orders.
senses.exampleCN: 这些食虫目科后来被拆散到多个目之中。
senses.why: Taxonomic adjectives follow the order name, so the food word became a formal classifier before the order was dissolved.
senses.whyCN: 分类学形容词跟着目名走，因此这个「食物词」在该目被撤销之前先成了一个正式分类标签。

senses.title: Built for an insect diet
senses.definition: describing teeth, jaws or guts shaped for catching and digesting insects
senses.definitionCN: 描述为捕捉与消化昆虫而演化出的牙齿、颌骨或消化道
senses.example: The fossil shows the insectivorous dentition typical of small nocturnal hunters.
senses.exampleCN: 这块化石显示出小型夜行捕食者典型的食虫齿列。
senses.why: Anatomy needs a word for structures that serve a diet, and the adjective attaches to the part rather than the whole animal.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学需要一个词来描述「为某种食性服务的结构」，形容词便附着在部位而不是整个动物身上。

senses.title: An ecological label
senses.definition: classifying a species by its membership in the insect-eating guild
senses.definitionCN: 按其在食虫功能群中的归属来分类物种
senses.example: The insectivorous birds shifted to fruit when caterpillars disappeared.
senses.exampleCN: 毛虫消失后，这些食虫鸟转而取食果实。
senses.why: Ecology uses adjectives to tag feeding roles quickly, so a species can be insectivorous in one season and not in another.
senses.whyCN: 生态学用形容词快速标注取食角色，因此同一物种在不同季节可以是食虫的，也可以不是。

senses.title: A pest-control ally
senses.definition: used of species valued because they suppress insect pests
senses.definitionCN: 用于指因抑制害虫而受重视的物种
senses.example: Farmers encourage insectivorous birds by keeping hedges and water.
senses.exampleCN: 农民保留树篱与水源，以招引食虫鸟。
senses.why: Applied writing converts the diet into a benefit, and the adjective marks the useful side of the same habit.
senses.whyCN: 应用写作把食性转化为效益，形容词标出的正是同一习性的有用一面。

senses.title: A trophic position
senses.definition: placed at the trophic level of consumers that feed on insects
senses.definitionCN: 处于以昆虫为食的消费者营养级
senses.example: Insectivorous fish link aquatic insects to larger predators.
senses.exampleCN: 食虫鱼类把水生昆虫连接到更大的捕食者。
senses.why: Food-web models need a level label, and the adjective marks where energy from insects enters the next trophic step.
senses.whyCN: 食物网模型需要一个层级标签，形容词标出的是昆虫的能量进入下一营养级的位置。

senses.title: Of peoples who eat insects
senses.definition: describing human communities whose traditional diet regularly includes insects
senses.definitionCN: 描述传统饮食中经常包含昆虫的人类群体
senses.example: Anthropologists documented insectivorous practices across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 人类学家记录了该地区各地的食虫习俗。
senses.why: The adjective's pattern extends to human groups, where it labels a cultural diet rather than a biological adaptation.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词的模式也延伸到人类群体，在那里标出的是文化性的饮食，而不是生物学适应。

intro.en: Insectivorous is the adjective built on insectivore, with a Latin ending that turns a noun of agent into a description.
intro.cn: insectivorous 是在 insectivore 基础上构成的形容词，用拉丁语词尾把「施动者名词」变成描述语。

items.en: The base is insectum, 'a thing cut into', plus vorare, 'to devour'. Both belonged to ordinary Latin before science borrowed them.
items.cn: 词基是 insectum「被切开的东西」加 vorare「吞食」。在被科学借用之前，这两个词都属于普通拉丁语。

items.en: The ending -ous continues Latin -osus, 'full of, characterized by'. It does not mean 'eating' by itself; the meaning is carried by the stem.
items.cn: 词尾 -ous 承自拉丁语 -osus「充满……的、以……为特征的」。它本身不表示「吃」，意义由词干承担。

items.en: Naturalists needed adjectives for diet-based groups, and insectivorous appeared alongside carnivorous and graminivorous in the same period.
items.cn: 博物学家需要为按食性划分的类群准备形容词，insectivorous 与 carnivorous、graminivorous 大约在同一时期出现。

items.en: Victorian botany popularized insectivorous plant after collectors brought back sundews and pitcher plants from tropical voyages.
items.cn: 维多利亚时代的植物学使 insectivorous plant 流行起来，当时采集者从热带航行带回茅膏菜与猪笼草。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology kept the adjective for functional and trophic labels, where diet is a role rather than a fixed identity.
items.cn: 20 世纪的生态学保留了这个形容词，用于功能群与营养级标签，此时食性是角色而非固定身份。

note.en: The first group is built from the same pieces; the second holds adjectives for other diets.
note.cn: 第一组由相同成分构成；第二组是表示其他食性的形容词。

entries.definition: The creature itself; insectivorous is the form that modifies bird, plant or dentition.
entries.definitionCN: 指生物本身；修饰 bird、plant、dentition 时要用 insectivorous。

entries.definition: The habit or diet, not a describer; you study insectivory but describe an insectivorous species.
entries.definitionCN: 指习性饮食，不是描述语；可以说研究 insectivory，但描述物种要用 insectivorous。

entries.definition: The food item; it says nothing about the eater's diet as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指食物本身，不说明取食者的整体食性。

entries.definition: Feeding on animal flesh; insects count as animal prey, so insectivorous is a narrow kind of carnivorous.
entries.definitionCN: 以动物肉体为食；昆虫也算动物性猎物，因此食虫是食肉的一种窄义。

entries.definition: Feeding on plants; the opposite dietary pole, though some insectivorous plants still photosynthesize.
entries.definitionCN: 以植物为食，是食性上的另一端；不过有些食虫植物仍进行光合作用。

entries.definition: Eating both plant and animal matter; such an animal may be insectivorous only part of the year.
entries.definitionCN: 动植物都吃；这类动物可能只在一年中的部分时间食虫。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the same Latin pieces seen from the adjective side.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：从形容词一侧看同一批拉丁语成分。

normal.en: -ous is the adjective switch: insectivore becomes insectivorous.
normal.cn: -ous 是形容词开关：insectivore 变成 insectivorous。

normal.en: The collocations mirror biology: insectivorous plant, bird, mammal, diet.
normal.cn: 搭配对应生物学场景：食虫植物、食虫鸟、食虫哺乳动物、食虫食性。

normal.en: The word sits in a family of diet adjectives: carnivorous, herbivorous, omnivorous.
normal.cn: 这个词属于一组食性形容词：carnivorous、herbivorous、omnivorous。

normal.en: A sundew is the clearest picture: a leaf that behaves like a stomach.
normal.cn: 茅膏菜是最清楚的画面：一片像胃一样工作的叶子。

normal.en: The first half is the prey, the second half is the eating; the ending says 'characterized by'.
normal.cn: 前半是猎物，后半是吃；词尾表示「以……为特征」。

abstract.en: Think of a restaurant whose only supplier is the insect world.
abstract.cn: 想象一家唯一供货商是昆虫世界的餐厅。

abstract.en: Picture a sticky doormat that punishes whoever steps on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块黏性门垫，谁踩上去谁就倒霉。

abstract.en: An insectivorous bird is a flying insect net that digests its catch.
abstract.cn: 食虫鸟就是一张会飞的昆虫网，还会把捕到的东西消化掉。

examples.en: Insectivorous birds help keep the orchard's caterpillars in check.
examples.cn: 食虫鸟有助于控制果园里的毛虫数量。

examples.en: The plant's insectivorous habit evolved in nutrient-poor bogs.
examples.cn: 这种植物的食虫习性是在养分贫乏的沼泽中演化出来的。

examples.en: Researchers compared the insectivorous diets of two bat species.
examples.cn: 研究者比较了两种蝙蝠的食虫食性。

dict_mnemonic.text: insect（昆虫）+ vor（吞）+ ous（……的）→ 吞昆虫的 → 食虫的

root: 拉丁语 insectum「昆虫」+ vorare「吞食」+ 形容词后缀 -ous（拉丁 -osus「充满……的」）→ insectivorous「以昆虫为食的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe the same property from different angles: the animal, the plant, the old order, the anatomy, the guild, the pest-control benefit, the trophic level and human communities.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从不同角度描述同一属性：动物、植物、旧分类目、解剖结构、功能群、害虫防治效益、营养级与人类群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a diet made of insects, attached to whatever lives on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：以昆虫构成的食谱，附着在任何靠它生活的生物身上。

branches.en: THE CORE: the adjective turns the noun insectivore into a property, whether the eater is an animal or an order member.
branches.cn: 核心：形容词把名词 insectivore 变成一种属性，无论取食者是动物还是旧目成员。

branches.en: THE PLANT: botany applies the same property to a photosynthesizing organism that traps prey.
branches.cn: 植物：植物学把同一属性用在一种仍进行光合作用、却能捕捉猎物的生物上。

branches.en: BODY AND LEVEL: the diet can be read from teeth or placed as a trophic position.
branches.cn: 身体与层级：食性既可以从牙齿读出，也能被放进营养级的位置。

branches.en: ROLE AND BENEFIT: ecology turns the diet into a guild label, and agriculture turns it into a service.
branches.cn: 角色与效益：生态学把食性变成功能群标签，农业把它变成一项服务。

branches.en: HUMANS: the same adjective can describe a cultural diet rather than a biological one.
branches.cn: 人类：同一形容词可以描述文化性的饮食，而不是生物学食性。

intro.en: Insectivorous is a three-part word: prey noun, eating root, descriptive ending.
intro.cn: insectivorous 由三部分组成：猎物名词、表示吃的词根、描述性词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are insectum and vorare, with the adjective ending -osus giving English -ous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 insectum 与 vorare，形容词词尾 -osus 在英语中变成 -ous。

items.example: The insectivorous bird nests in hollow trees.
items.exampleCN: 这种食虫鸟在空心树里筑巢。

items.example: The insectivore stores fat for the cold months.
items.exampleCN: 这种食虫动物为寒冷月份储存脂肪。

items.example: Insectivory is common among small tropical birds.
items.exampleCN: 食虫习性在小型热带鸟类中很常见。

items.example: Carnivorous plants trap more than insects.
items.exampleCN: 食肉植物捕捉的不只是昆虫。

items.example: Herbivorous insects strip the leaves in weeks.
items.exampleCN: 食草昆虫几周内就能把叶子吃光。

items.example: The nestlings have voracious appetites.
items.exampleCN: 雏鸟的食量很大。

items.example: The trap catches insects by smell.
items.exampleCN: 这个诱捕器靠气味捕捉昆虫。

items.example: The label warns that the insecticide harms bees.
items.exampleCN: 标签警告这种杀虫剂会伤害蜜蜂。

definition_zh: 食腐动物；拾荒者；清除剂
definition_en: an animal or person that feeds on what others have left behind, especially dead matter
core_image: 一只秃鹫落在尸体旁，把别人不要的剩肉吃干净
scene: Vultures act as scavengers, stripping a carcass before disease can spread.
sceneCN: 这里 scavenger 是「食腐动物」（第 1 个义项：以动物尸体为食的动物）；句意：秃鹫充当食腐动物，在疾病扩散之前把尸体清理干净。

pos.zh: 食腐动物；拾荒者；清道夫；清除剂（可数，复数 scavengers）

derivatives.zh: 寻宝游戏（收集物品的活动）

senses.title: An animal that eats carrion
senses.definition: an animal that feeds on the dead bodies or remains of other animals
senses.definitionCN: 以其他动物尸体或残骸为食的动物
senses.example: Wolves often work as scavengers in winter, feeding on kills they did not make.
senses.exampleCN: 狼在冬季常充当食腐者，取食并非自己捕杀的猎物。
senses.why: The word labels an animal by what it takes from others' leftovers, so the diet is defined by the source rather than the species.
senses.whyCN: 这个词按「从别人剩余物中取食」来给动物分类，因此食性由食物来源定义，而不是由物种定义。

senses.title: A large carrion bird
senses.definition: specifically, a bird such as a vulture or a crow that locates and consumes carcasses
senses.definitionCN: 特指秃鹫、乌鸦等能发现并取食尸体的鸟类
senses.example: The vulture's bare head is an adaptation of a dedicated scavenger.
senses.exampleCN: 秃鹫裸露的头是专职食腐者的一种适应。
senses.why: Large birds are the most visible scavengers, so the general noun often points to them without further qualification.
senses.whyCN: 大型鸟类是最显眼的食腐者，因此这个普通名词常常不加限定就指向它们。

senses.title: A person who picks through waste
senses.definition: a person who collects usable material from discarded waste
senses.definitionCN: 从废弃物品中收集可用材料的人
senses.example: Scavengers sorted bottles and metal from the landfill edge.
senses.exampleCN: 拾荒者在垃圾填埋场边缘分拣瓶子和金属。
senses.why: Human waste-picking repeats the animal pattern of living on what others discard, so the same word moved from carcasses to rubbish.
senses.whyCN: 人类拾荒重复了动物「靠别人丢弃物生活」的模式，于是同一个词从尸体移到了垃圾。

senses.title: A street cleaner
senses.definition: historically, a worker or vehicle employed to clean streets and remove refuse
senses.definitionCN: 历史上受雇清扫街道、清运垃圾的工人或车辆
senses.example: The medieval scavenger was a paid official, not a beggar.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的 scavenger 是有薪的官吏，而不是乞丐。
senses.why: The word's oldest English sense is institutional, naming the officer who kept streets clear; the animal sense came later.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在英语中最古老的意思是制度性的，指负责保持街道清洁的官员；动物义项出现得更晚。

senses.title: A cleaner of the ecosystem
senses.definition: an organism whose feeding removes dead organic matter and recycles its nutrients
senses.definitionCN: 通过取食清除死亡有机物并回收养分的生物
senses.example: Beetles and flies are the small scavengers that clear the forest floor.
senses.exampleCN: 甲虫和蝇类是清理森林地表的小型食腐者。
senses.why: Ecology reframes the eater as a service: consuming dead matter is how nutrients return to the system.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把取食者重新描述为一项服务：吃掉死去的物质，正是养分回到系统的方式。

senses.title: A chemical remover
senses.definition: a substance that removes unwanted molecules, such as free radicals or impurities
senses.definitionCN: 除去不需要的分子（如自由基或杂质）的物质
senses.example: Vitamin C serves as a scavenger of free radicals in the cell.
senses.exampleCN: 维生素 C 在细胞中充当自由基清除剂。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the image of something sweeping leftovers away, and the target became reactive molecules instead of meat.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用了「把剩余物扫走」的形象，被清扫的对象从肉变成了活性分子。

senses.title: An industrial clean-up device
senses.definition: equipment or a process that removes waste gases or residues from a stream
senses.definitionCN: 从气流或液流中除去废气或残渣的设备或工艺
senses.example: The scrubber works as a scavenger for sulphur compounds in the exhaust.
senses.exampleCN: 洗涤器充当废气中硫化合物的清除装置。
senses.why: Industry applies the same removal idea to flows of gas and liquid, so the word can name a machine as well as a substance.
senses.whyCN: 工业把同样的「清除」思路用到气液流动上，因此这个词既能指物质，也能指设备。

senses.title: One who lives off leftovers
senses.titleCN: 靠他人剩余物生活的人
senses.definition: figuratively, a person who takes advantage of what others leave unused or abandoned
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指利用他人未用或弃置之物的人
senses.example: Critics called the middlemen scavengers of the industry's failed projects.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把这些中间商称为该行业失败项目的拾荒者。
senses.why: The literal image of feeding on remains supplies a moral metaphor for opportunism, without changing the core relation.
senses.whyCN: 「以残余为食」的字面形象为机会主义提供了一种道德隐喻，而核心关系并未改变。

intro.en: Scavenger began as a customs and street officer, then slid into the animal that cleans up carcasses.
intro.cn: scavenger 起初指海关与街道官吏，后来滑向「清理尸体的动物」这一义项。

items.en: The word traces to Anglo-French scawage, a toll or charge on goods, and scawager, the officer who collected it and inspected streets. The ultimate source is usually taken to be a Frankish verb meaning 'to look at', reconstructed as skauwon; that form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 这个词上溯至盎格鲁-法语 scawage「货物税」与 scawager「收税并巡查街道的官吏」。其最终来源一般认为是一个表示「看」的法兰克语动词，重构形式作 skauwon；这一形式属于重构，并非有记录的词。

items.en: English adopted scavager in the sixteenth century. The ending was later remodeled to -enger, as in messenger, producing scavenger.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 scavager。词尾后来被改造成 -enger（如 messenger），于是产生了 scavenger。

items.en: For centuries a scavenger was a paid official who kept streets clear of refuse, a sense still recorded in historical writing.
items.cn: 在数百年间，scavenger 指受雇保持街道无垃圾的官吏，这一义项在历史写作中仍有记录。

items.en: The ecological sense, an animal living on carrion, becomes common in the nineteenth century with the rise of natural history writing. The exact first use is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 指以腐肉为生的动物这一生态义项，随 19 世纪博物学写作的兴起而常见。确切首见年代尚无定论。

items.en: Twentieth-century chemistry extended scavenger to substances that remove free radicals or impurities, and industry to clean-up devices.
items.cn: 20 世纪的化学把这个词扩展到除去自由基或杂质的物质，工业界则扩展到净化装置。

note.en: The first group shares the root; the second holds other feeders and cleaners.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一词根；第二组是其他取食者与清理者。

entries.definition: The action of feeding on remains or searching waste; scavenger is the one that does it.
entries.definitionCN: 指食腐或翻找废弃物的动作；scavenger 指实施这一动作的生物。

entries.definition: Names the activity or describes it; it never names the animal itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指这项活动或作定语描述，不能直接指动物本身。

entries.definition: Describes what has been picked over, as in scavenged bone; it marks the object, not the eater.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已被翻找过的对象，如被啃食过的骨头；它标记的是对象，不是取食者。

entries.definition: An animal that eats detritus, mostly dead plant fragments; scavenger usually points to animal carcasses.
entries.definitionCN: 以腐屑（多为死亡植物碎片）为食的动物；scavenger 通常指取食动物尸体。

entries.definition: A bacterium or fungus that breaks matter down chemically; a scavenger eats and digests, a decomposer mineralizes.
entries.definitionCN: 通过化学方式分解物质的细菌或真菌；食腐者取食消化，分解者则把物质矿化。

entries.definition: An animal that hunts live prey; a scavenger takes what is already dead.
entries.definitionCN: 捕杀活猎物的动物；食腐者取食已经死去的动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real relatives, real phrases and the historical street sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实同族词、真实搭配与历史上的街道义项。

normal.en: The verb is scavenge; the activity is scavenging; the actor is scavenger.
normal.cn: 动词是 scavenge，活动是 scavenging，施行者是 scavenger。

normal.en: The word began as a street officer, which explains why it can still mean a cleaner.
normal.cn: 这个词最初指街道官吏，这也解释了它为何仍可表示「清扫者」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases reveal the range: carrion scavenger, scavenger hunt, free-radical scavenger.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出词义范围：食腐尸动物、寻宝游戏、自由基清除剂。

normal.en: A vulture on a carcass is the default picture of the word.
normal.cn: 秃鹫立在尸体旁，是这个词最典型的画面。

normal.en: The -enger ending also appears in messenger and harbinger, all old agent nouns.
normal.cn: -enger 词尾也出现在 messenger 与 harbinger 中，都是古老的施动名词。

abstract.en: Think of a city's night crew: nobody produces the rubbish, but someone must clear it.
abstract.cn: 想象城市的夜班工人：垃圾不是他们制造的，但总得有人清走。

abstract.en: A scavenger is a recycling plant that walks.
abstract.cn: 食腐者就是一座会走路的回收厂。

abstract.en: In chemistry the same word is a sweeper that removes what the reaction does not want.
abstract.cn: 在化学里，同一个词是清扫工，专门清走反应不想要的东西。

examples.en: Scavengers such as jackals can move nutrients across a whole valley.
examples.cn: 像豺这样的食腐动物能把养分搬运到整片山谷。

examples.en: The antioxidant acts as a scavenger of damaging radicals.
examples.cn: 这种抗氧化剂充当有害自由基的清除剂。

examples.en: City records show that a scavenger was paid to clear the market square.
examples.cn: 城市档案显示，曾有一位清扫官吏受雇清理集市广场。

dict_mnemonic.text: scav（谐音「死尸」）+ enger → 处理死尸的人 → 食腐动物、拾荒者

root: 盎格鲁-法语 scawager「收税并巡查街道的官吏」，来自 scawage「货物税」；其更早来源一般认为是一个表示「看」的法兰克语动词（重构形式 *skauwōn），属于重构而非确证词形。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: living on what others leave. The eater may be an animal, a person, a chemical or a machine, but the relation stays the same.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个想法展开：靠别人留下的东西生活。取食者可以是动物、人、化学物质或机器，但那个关系始终不变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a consumer that lives on remains others abandon.
core.cn: 核心意象：靠他人弃置的残余为生的取食者。

branches.en: THE CORE: dead bodies supply the food, and large birds make the pattern most visible.
branches.cn: 核心：尸体提供食物，大型鸟类让这一模式最显眼。

branches.en: HUMAN WASTE: people who pick through rubbish repeat the animal relation, while the oldest sense is the paid street officer.
branches.cn: 人类废弃物：翻拣垃圾的人重复了动物的关系，而最古老义项则是受薪的街道官吏。

branches.en: THE SERVICE: ecology reads carrion eating as nutrient recycling, not as theft.
branches.cn: 服务：生态学把食腐读作养分循环，而不是「偷食」。

branches.en: THE MOLECULE: chemistry retargets the sweeping action from flesh to radicals and impurities.
branches.cn: 分子：化学把清扫动作的对象从肉体改成自由基与杂质。

branches.en: MACHINE AND METAPHOR: industry builds devices that scavenge exhaust, and critics use the word for opportunists.
branches.cn: 机器与隐喻：工业造出清除废气的装置，批评者则用这个词指机会主义者。

intro.en: Scavenger is an old agent noun whose ending was reshaped by English speakers; its parts are no longer transparent.
intro.cn: scavenger 是一个古老的施动名词，词尾经英语使用者改造，其构件已不再透明。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved. The base is Anglo-French scawage, with a Germanic source usually reconstructed as Frankish skauwon; the English -enger ending is by analogy with messenger.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词不涉及拉丁词根。词基是盎格鲁-法语 scawage，其日耳曼语来源一般重构为法兰克语 skauwon；英语词尾 -enger 是类比 messenger 改造而来。

items.example: The beetle is a scavenger of the forest floor.
items.exampleCN: 这种甲虫是森林地表的食腐者。

items.meaning: to feed on remains or search waste
items.example: Rats scavenge around the bins at night.
items.exampleCN: 老鼠夜间在垃圾桶周围觅食。

items.meaning: the activity of living on remains
items.example: Scavenging by gulls increases near landfills.
items.exampleCN: 垃圾填埋场附近海鸥的拾食活动会增加。

items.meaning: picked over or removed as waste
items.meaningCN: 被翻拣过的；作为废弃物被清除的
items.example: The scavenged carcass was reduced to bones.
items.exampleCN: 被啃食过的尸体只剩下骨头。

items.example: Messenger and scavenger share the reshaped ending.
items.exampleCN: messenger 与 scavenger 共享这个被改造的词尾。

items.meaning: one that announces what is coming
items.example: The first frost is a harbinger of winter.
items.exampleCN: 初霜是冬天将至的预兆。

items.example: Carrion attracts a crowd of scavengers.
items.exampleCN: 腐肉招来一群食腐动物。

items.example: The street officer removed refuse each morning.
items.exampleCN: 街道官吏每天早晨清走垃圾。

definition_en: the activity of feeding on remains or of removing what is unwanted
core_image: 一只动物沿着海岸线翻找被浪潮留下的死鱼
scene: Scavenging by gulls increases sharply near open landfills.
sceneCN: 这里 scavenging 是「食腐、拾食」（第 1 个义项：动物取食尸体或残余的行为）；句意：在露天垃圾场附近，海鸥的拾食行为明显增加。

pos.zh: 食腐；拾荒；清扫；清除（不可数，作动名词）
食腐的；拾荒的；清除用的（作定语）

derivatives.zh: 食腐动物；拾荒者；清除剂

senses.title: Feeding on carcasses
senses.definition: the activity of animals feeding on dead bodies or abandoned remains
senses.definitionCN: 动物取食尸体或弃置残余的活动
senses.example: Night-time scavenging exposes foxes to poisoned carcasses.
senses.exampleCN: 夜间食腐使狐狸接触到被下毒的尸体。
senses.why: The -ing form names the activity rather than the actor, so the focus falls on how the food is obtained.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式命名的是活动而不是施动者，因此重点落在「食物是如何获得的」。

senses.title: Picking through waste
senses.definition: the practice of collecting usable material from discarded waste
senses.definitionCN: 从废弃物品中收集可用材料的做法
senses.example: Scavenging at the dump supports a small informal economy.
senses.exampleCN: 在垃圾场拾荒支撑起一个小型的非正规经济。
senses.why: People repeat the animal pattern with rubbish instead of carcasses, and the activity noun covers both.
senses.whyCN: 人用垃圾代替尸体重复了动物的模式，而这个活动名词把两者都涵盖进来。

senses.title: Street cleaning
senses.definition: the historical duty of keeping streets clear of refuse
senses.definitionCN: 历史上保持街道无垃圾的职责
senses.example: Records list payments for scavenging in the market ward.
senses.exampleCN: 档案中列有集市街区清扫工作的支出。
senses.why: Before it named animal behaviour, the word named a municipal job, and the activity noun preserves that administrative sense.
senses.whyCN: 在指动物行为之前，这个词指的是市政职务，活动名词保留了这层行政含义。

senses.title: Clearing dead matter
senses.titleCN: 清除死亡有机物的生态过程
senses.definition: the ecological process by which animals remove dead organic matter and release its nutrients
senses.definitionCN: 动物清除死亡有机物并释放其养分的生态过程
senses.example: Scavenging speeds up nutrient return in the savanna.
senses.exampleCN: 食腐加快了稀树草原上养分的回归。
senses.why: Ecology treats the activity as a process with an effect on the system, not merely as a feeding habit.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把这项活动看作对系统产生影响的过程，而不只是取食习性。

senses.title: Removing reactive molecules
senses.definition: in chemistry, the removal of free radicals or other reactive species
senses.definitionCN: 化学中除去自由基或其他活性物种的过程
senses.example: The assay measures radical scavenging by the plant extract.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测定测量植物提取物的自由基清除能力。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the sweeping image and applied it to molecules that damage cells.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用了「清扫」的形象，把它用在会损伤细胞的分子上。

senses.title: Cleaning a gas or liquid stream
senses.definition: in industry, the removal of unwanted gases, oxygen or residues from a process stream
senses.definitionCN: 工业中从工艺物流中除去不需要的气体、氧气或残渣
senses.example: Oxygen scavenging protects the boiler from corrosion.
senses.exampleCN: 除氧处理保护锅炉免受腐蚀。
senses.why: The same removal idea becomes a unit operation, so the activity noun names a stage in a plant.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「清除」思路变成一道单元操作，活动名词因此指工厂中的一个环节。

senses.title: Collecting supplies in a game
senses.definition: in gaming and outdoor parlance, the search for useful items left in a world or landscape
senses.definitionCN: 在游戏与户外语境中，搜寻场景里留下的可用物品
senses.example: Scavenging for ammo slowed the squad's advance.
senses.exampleCN: 搜刮弹药拖慢了小队的推进。
senses.why: Digital worlds reproduce the same loop of finding what is left behind, so players adopted the existing word.
senses.whyCN: 虚拟世界重现了「找到别人留下的东西」这一循环，于是玩家沿用了现成的词。

senses.title: Living off others' leavings
senses.definition: figuratively, profiting from what others have discarded or overlooked
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指从他人丢弃或忽视的东西中获利
senses.example: Critics described the firm's scavenging in the ruins of failed startups.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把这家公司蚕食失败初创企业残局的行为称为 scavenging。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the core relation intact: gain comes from what someone else no longer uses.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻保持了核心关系：收益来自别人已不再使用的东西。

intro.en: Scavenging is the -ing form of scavenge, a verb back-formed from scavenger, the old street officer.
intro.cn: scavenging 是 scavenge 的 -ing 形式，而 scavenge 是从古老的街道官吏 scavenger 反向构成的动词。

items.en: Scavenge appeared later than scavenger. English speakers clipped the noun's ending and made a verb, a common pattern in English word formation.
items.cn: scavenge 比 scavenger 出现得晚。英语使用者把名词词尾截短造出动词，这是英语构词的常见方式。

items.en: Scavenger goes back to Anglo-French scawager, an officer who collected a toll and inspected streets; the underlying scawage meant such a toll. The deeper Germanic source is usually reconstructed, not recorded.
items.cn: scavenger 上溯至盎格鲁-法语 scawager，指收取货物税并巡查街道的官吏；其词基 scawage 指这项税。更早的日耳曼语来源属重构，并非有记录的形式。

items.en: English forms verbal nouns in -ing freely, so once the verb existed, scavenging could name the activity in any domain.
items.cn: 英语可以自由地用 -ing 构成动名词，因此动词一出现，scavenging 就能在任何领域命名这项活动。

items.en: Naturalists applied the word to animals living on carrion, and the activity sense became standard in descriptions of feeding behaviour.
items.cn: 博物学家把这个词用于以腐肉为生的动物，活动义项随之成为取食行为描述中的标准用法。

items.en: Chemistry, engineering and later gaming each adopted scavenging for their own version of removing or collecting leftovers. The core sense never changed.
items.cn: 化学、工程以及后来的游戏领域各自采用 scavenging，指各自版本的「清除或收集剩余物」。核心义始终未变。

note.en: The first group is the same word family in other forms; the second holds related processes.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族的其他形式；第二组是相关过程。

entries.definition: The animal or person that does the activity; scavenging is what it does.
entries.definitionCN: 实施该活动的动物或人；scavenging 是它做的事。

entries.definition: The plain verb, used after to or with a subject; the -ing form can be a noun, which the verb cannot.
entries.definitionCN: 动词原形，用于 to 之后或带主语；-ing 形式可作名词，动词原形不能。

entries.definition: Describes what has already been picked over; it marks the object or completed action.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已被翻拣过的对象，标记对象或已完成的动作。

entries.definition: The general search for food; scavenging narrows it to food already dead or discarded.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指搜寻食物；scavenging 窄化为搜寻已死或被弃的食物。

entries.definition: The chemical breakdown of matter; scavenging removes remains, decomposition transforms them.
entries.definitionCN: 物质的化学分解；食腐是移走残余，分解是转化残余。

entries.definition: Processing waste into new material; scavenging only collects, without industrial reprocessing.
entries.definitionCN: 把废弃物加工成新材料；拾荒只收集，不做工业再加工。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the verb family and the visible activity.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：动词词族与可见的活动。

normal.en: scavenge is the verb, scavenger the actor, scavenging the activity.
normal.cn: scavenge 是动词，scavenger 是施动者，scavenging 是活动。

normal.en: The collocations split into biological and technical: scavenging behavior, free-radical scavenging.
normal.cn: 搭配分为生物与技术两类：食腐行为、自由基清除。

normal.en: The word is old enough to have meant street sweeping before it meant carrion eating.
normal.cn: 这个词足够古老，在表示「食腐」之前先表示「扫街」。

normal.en: A gull on a landfill is the modern picture; a vulture on a carcass is the old one.
normal.cn: 垃圾场上的海鸥是当代画面；尸体旁的秃鹫是古老画面。

normal.en: The -ing noun works anywhere a leftover is removed, from cells to software worlds.
normal.cn: 只要有「剩余物被清走」的地方，这个 -ing 名词都适用，从细胞到虚拟世界。

abstract.en: Think of a beachcombing walk: the sea decides what is available, you only collect it.
abstract.cn: 想象一次海滩拾荒：海决定有什么，你只负责捡。

abstract.en: A white blood cell scavenging radicals is a street sweeper at molecular scale.
abstract.cn: 清除自由基的白细胞，就是分子尺度的环卫工。

abstract.en: In a game, every empty room is a chance to scavenge; in a forest, every carcass is.
abstract.cn: 在游戏里，每间空房都是搜刮机会；在森林里，每具尸体都是。

examples.en: Scavenging by crabs removes dead fish before they foul the water.
examples.cn: 螃蟹的食腐在死鱼污染水体之前就把它们清走。

examples.en: The antioxidant's scavenging capacity was measured in the laboratory.
examples.cn: 这种抗氧化剂的清除能力在实验室中进行了测定。

examples.en: Oxygen scavenging is standard practice in boiler maintenance.
examples.cn: 除氧是锅炉维护中的标准做法。

dict_mnemonic.text: scavenge（读音近「死该焚尸」）+ ing → 处理尸体 → 食腐、拾荒

root: 由 scavenger（盎格鲁-法语 scawager「收税并巡查街道的官吏」）反向构成动词 scavenge，再加 -ing；更早的日耳曼语来源一般重构为法兰克语 *skauwōn「看」，属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses name the same activity in different worlds: carrion, rubbish, streets, ecosystems, cells, plants, games and business.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在不同世界里命名同一项活动：尸体、垃圾、街道、生态系统、细胞、工厂、游戏与商业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an ongoing search that turns leftovers into a living.
core.cn: 核心意象：一场持续的搜寻，把剩余物变成生计。

branches.en: THE CORE: animals and people both live by finding what has been left, whether flesh or rubbish.
branches.cn: 核心：动物与人同样靠「找到被留下的东西」生活，无论那是肉还是垃圾。

branches.en: THE OLD JOB: the municipal sense survives mainly in historical writing.
branches.cn: 古老职业：市政义项主要保存在历史写作中。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: ecology studies the activity for its effect on nutrient flow.
branches.cn: 过程：生态学研究这项活动对养分流动的影响。

branches.en: THE TECHNOLOGY: chemistry and industry remove molecules and gases with the same sweeping image.
branches.cn: 技术：化学与工业用同一个「清扫」形象来清除分子与气体。

branches.en: THE EXTENSIONS: games make collection a mechanic, and critics make it a moral charge.
branches.cn: 延伸：游戏把收集变成机制，批评者把它变成道德指控。

intro.en: Scavenging is a verb stem plus the productive English ending -ing.
intro.cn: scavenging 是动词词干加上高产的英语词尾 -ing。

latinIntro.en: No Latin component is present. The base is Anglo-French, with a Germanic source usually reconstructed as Frankish skauwon.
latinIntro.cn: 其中没有拉丁语成分。词基来自盎格鲁-法语，其日耳曼语来源一般重构为法兰克语 skauwon。

items.meaning: the activity of living on remains
items.example: Scavenging is common among urban foxes.
items.exampleCN: 食腐在城市狐狸中很常见。

items.meaning: to feed on or collect leftovers
items.example: Birds scavenge along the tide line.
items.exampleCN: 鸟类沿着潮线觅食。

items.example: The crow is an opportunistic scavenger.
items.exampleCN: 乌鸦是机会主义的食腐者。

items.example: The scavenged remains were mostly bone.
items.exampleCN: 被啃食后的残余大多是骨头。

items.example: Carrion attracts nocturnal scavenging.
items.exampleCN: 腐肉招来夜间的食腐活动。

items.structure: Old French waste, from Latin vastum
items.example: Waste picking is a form of human scavenging.
items.exampleCN: 拾荒是人类食腐式活动的一种形式。

items.example: Forage is the broader verb that scavenging narrows.
items.exampleCN: forage 是更宽的动词，scavenging 是它的窄化形式。

items.example: Refuse collection replaced the old scavenging duty.
items.exampleCN: 垃圾清运取代了旧的清扫职责。

definition_en: the process of breaking something down into simpler parts or substances
core_image: 一块落叶在土里慢慢裂成看不见的碎片
scene: Bacterial decomposition turns the fallen leaves into dark soil within a year.
sceneCN: 这里 decomposition 是「分解、腐烂」（第 2 个义项：有机物被微生物分解）；句意：细菌分解在一年之内把落叶变成深色土壤。

pos.zh: 分解；腐烂；降解；拆解（不可数，特定语境可作可数）

derivatives.zh: 组成；作品；构成（同词根反向词）

senses.title: Breaking a compound apart
senses.definition: a chemical reaction in which a compound splits into simpler substances
senses.definitionCN: 化合物裂解为更简单物质的化学反应
senses.example: Heating limestone causes the decomposition of calcium carbonate.
senses.exampleCN: 加热石灰石会导致碳酸钙分解。
senses.why: de- means apart and composition means putting together, so the noun names the undoing of a chemical combination.
senses.whyCN: de- 表示「分开」，composition 表示「放在一起」，因此这个名词指把化学组合拆开。

senses.title: Rotting of dead matter
senses.definition: the process by which dead plants or animals decay into simpler matter
senses.definitionCN: 死亡动植物腐烂为更简单物质的过程
senses.example: Decomposition of the fallen log took nearly a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这根倒木的分解花了将近十年。
senses.why: Living bodies are built from compounds, so their decay is chemically the same undoing of combinations.
senses.whyCN: 活体由化合物构成，因此它们的腐败在化学上就是同样的「拆解组合」。

senses.title: An ecosystem process
senses.definition: the ecological process that returns carbon and nutrients from dead matter to the environment
senses.definitionCN: 把碳与养分从死亡有机物归还环境的生态过程
senses.example: Decomposition in tropical soils is fast because of heat and moisture.
senses.exampleCN: 热带土壤中的分解因高温与湿润而很快。
senses.why: Ecology treats the same chemistry as a system function, measured by rates and nutrient budgets.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把同一套化学当作系统功能，用速率与养分收支来衡量。

senses.title: Breaking down a mathematical object
senses.definition: the splitting of a function, matrix or graph into simpler components
senses.definitionCN: 把函数、矩阵或图拆成更简单成分
senses.example: The algorithm relies on a matrix decomposition that costs little memory.
senses.exampleCN: 该算法依赖一种占用内存很少的矩阵分解。
senses.why: Mathematics borrows the word because the operation is literally a structured breaking-apart of a whole.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用这个词，因为该操作确实是把整体按结构拆开。

senses.title: Splitting a system into modules
senses.definition: in computing, the division of a problem or system into smaller independent parts
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域把问题或系统划分为更小的独立部分
senses.example: Good decomposition keeps each module testable on its own.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的系统拆分让每个模块都能独立测试。
senses.why: Software design repeats the chemical image at a higher level: a complex whole is easier to handle in parts.
senses.whyCN: 软件设计在更高层次重复了化学的意象：复杂的整体拆成部分更好处理。

senses.title: Taking an argument apart
senses.definition: the analytical separation of a text, argument or idea into its components
senses.definitionCN: 把文本、论证或观点分析性地拆成若干成分
senses.example: Her decomposition of the speech showed how the argument shifted halfway.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这篇演讲的拆解显示出论证在中途如何转向。
senses.why: Analysis is mental decomposition, and the noun marks the structured separation rather than the decay.
senses.whyCN: 分析就是心智上的分解，这个名词标记的是有条理的拆分，而不是腐败。

senses.title: Stages after death
senses.definition: in forensic science, the sequence of changes by which a body breaks down after death
senses.definitionCN: 法医学中尸体死后逐步崩解的阶段序列
senses.example: Insect evidence placed the decomposition stage at about two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 昆虫证据把这一分解阶段判断在两周左右。
senses.why: Forensic taphonomy needs a neutral word for the whole sequence, avoiding the vaguer everyday term decay.
senses.whyCN: 法医埋藏学需要一个中性的词来描述整个序列，避开含混的日常词 decay。

senses.title: Release of nutrients
senses.definition: the release of soluble nutrients into soil or water as dead matter breaks down
senses.definitionCN: 死亡有机物崩解时把可溶养分释放到土壤或水中
senses.example: Decomposition released enough nitrate to feed the next crop.
senses.exampleCN: 分解释放的硝酸盐足以供养下一季作物。
senses.why: This sense focuses on the output rather than the process, since the breakdown is valued for what it gives back.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项聚焦于产出而非过程，因为人们看重分解，正是看重它归还了什么。

intro.en: Decomposition undoes a Latin putting-together; the English word may have been borrowed from French rather than built in English.
intro.cn: decomposition 把拉丁语的「放在一起」拆开；这个英语词可能借自法语，而不是在英语内部构造的。

items.en: Composition comes from Latin componere, 'to put together', made of com- 'together' and ponere 'to place'. The root ponere also yields position, deposit and impose.
items.cn: composition 来自拉丁语 componere「放在一起」，由 com-「共同」与 ponere「放置」构成。词根 ponere 还产生 position、deposit 与 impose。

items.en: The prefix de- here means 'down, apart, away', the same reversal force it has in detach and decline.
items.cn: 此处前缀 de- 表示「向下、分开、离开」，与它在 detach、decline 中的反转意味相同。

items.en: French chemists formed decomposer in the eighteenth century for the separation of compound substances. English decompose and decomposition followed, probably through French rather than directly from Latin.
items.cn: 法国化学家在 18 世纪造出 decomposer，用于描述化合物物质的分离。英语的 decompose 与 decomposition 随之出现，大概是经法语而不是直接从拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: With the rise of ecology, decomposition was applied to the decay of dead organisms and the cycling of nutrients. The exact date of this shift is not firmly established.
items.cn: 随着生态学兴起，decomposition 被用于描述死亡有机体的腐败与养分循环。这一转变的确切年代尚无定论。

items.en: Twentieth-century mathematics and computing extended the word to the structured splitting of matrices, functions, systems and problems.
items.cn: 20 世纪的数学与计算把这个词扩展到矩阵、函数、系统与问题的结构化拆分。

note.en: The first group is built on the same root; the second holds related breakdown processes.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一词根上；第二组是相关的崩解过程。

entries.definition: The action itself; decomposition is the process noun derived from it.
entries.definitionCN: 指动作本身；decomposition 是由它派生的过程名词。

entries.definition: The putting together of parts, or the resulting whole; decomposition undoes exactly that.
entries.definitionCN: 把部分放在一起，或由此形成的整体；decomposition 正是把这一过程反过来。

entries.definition: An organism or device that carries out decomposition; the noun ending -er marks the actor.
entries.definitionCN: 执行分解的生物或装置；-er 词尾标记施动者。

entries.definition: Slow natural rotting, often with a negative tone; decomposition is the neutral scientific term.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢的自然腐烂，常带负面色彩；decomposition 是中性科学术语。

entries.definition: A general failure or separation, usable for machines, health or chemistry; decomposition is more specific.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指故障或分离，可用于机器、健康或化学；decomposition 更具体。

entries.definition: Anaerobic rotting of protein-rich matter with a strong smell; a narrower, more graphic kind of decomposition.
entries.definitionCN: 富含蛋白质的物质在缺氧条件下的腐烂，气味强烈；是分解中更窄、更具体的一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the de-/com- reversal and the scientific collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：de- 与 com- 的反向关系以及科学搭配。

normal.en: composition puts together; decomposition takes apart. The prefixes do the work.
normal.cn: composition 把东西放在一起，decomposition 把它们拆开，起作用的是两个前缀。

normal.en: The family runs decompose, decomposer, decomposable, decomposition.
normal.cn: 同族词有 decompose、decomposer、decomposable、decomposition。

normal.en: Standard phrases mark the fields: organic decomposition, thermal decomposition, rate of decomposition.
normal.cn: 标准搭配标出领域：有机物分解、热分解、分解速率。

normal.en: The root ponere 'place' also hides in position, deposit and impose.
normal.cn: 词根 ponere「放置」也藏在 position、deposit、impose 里。

normal.en: A leaf turning into soil is the image that fits both the garden and the laboratory.
normal.cn: 叶子变成土壤的画面，既适合花园，也适合实验室。

abstract.en: Think of a Lego castle being taken apart brick by brick, with each brick still usable.
abstract.cn: 想象一座乐高城堡被一块块拆开，每块砖仍能继续使用。

abstract.en: A fallen tree is a bank account that decomposition pays out slowly.
abstract.cn: 倒下的树是一个账户，分解在慢慢把存款付出去。

abstract.en: In code, decomposition is the same gesture: a big block split into pieces you can carry.
abstract.cn: 在代码里，分解是同一个动作：把大块拆成你能拿得动的小块。

examples.en: The rate of decomposition depends on temperature, water and oxygen.
examples.cn: 分解速率取决于温度、水分与氧气。

examples.en: Thermal decomposition of the sample released a colourless gas.
examples.cn: 样品的热分解释放出一种无色气体。

examples.en: The team's decomposition of the problem made the code far easier to test.
examples.cn: 团队对问题的拆分使代码更容易测试。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（去掉）+ composition（组合）→ 把组合拆掉 → 分解、腐烂

root: 拉丁语 de-「分开、向下」+ compositio「组合」，后者来自 componere（com-「共同」+ ponere「放置」）；经法语 décomposer 进入英语，形成 decompose 与 decomposition。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a whole coming apart: a compound, a body, an ecosystem, a matrix, a system, a text, a corpse, a nutrient store.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述「整体拆开」：化合物、尸体、生态系统、矩阵、系统、文本、遗体、养分库。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a structured whole losing its bonds and falling into simpler pieces.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个有结构的整体失去结合，散成更简单的碎片。

branches.en: THE CORE: a chemical combination is undone, whether in a flask or in a dead body.
branches.cn: 核心：化学组合被拆开，无论是在烧瓶里还是在尸体里。

branches.en: THE ECOSYSTEM: the process is studied for its rate and for the nutrients it releases.
branches.cn: 生态系统：人们研究这一过程的速率，以及它释放的养分。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: mathematics splits functions, matrices and graphs into simpler parts.
branches.cn: 对象：数学把函数、矩阵与图拆成更简单的部分。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: computing splits problems into modules that can be handled separately.
branches.cn: 系统：计算把问题拆成可分别处理的模块。

branches.en: THE READING: an argument can be taken apart for analysis, and a corpse for forensic reconstruction.
branches.cn: 解读：论证可被拆解以供分析，尸体可被拆解以供法医重建。

intro.en: Decomposition is a prefix of reversal plus a noun of putting together.
intro.cn: decomposition 是一个表示反转的前缀加上一个表示「组合」的名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are de- 'apart' and componere 'to put together' (com- + ponere 'place'), with the noun ending -itio giving English -ition.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 de-「分开」与 componere「放在一起」（com- + ponere「放置」），名词词尾 -itio 在英语中变为 -ition。

items.example: The packaging is fully decomposable in soil.

items.meaning: a putting together; the whole so formed

items.meaning: a place where something is set

items.exampleCN: position 与 composition 共享一个拉丁词根。

items.example: The river deposit holds partly decomposed matter.

definition_en: to break something down into simpler parts or substances
core_image: 一块木头在湿土里一年年变软、变空、最后消失
scene: Fungi decompose the fallen trunk until only a dark line of soil remains.
sceneCN: 这里 decompose 是「分解、腐烂」（第 2 个义项：有机物被真菌分解）；句意：真菌分解这根倒下的树干，最后只剩一道深色的土痕。

pos.zh: 使分解；使腐烂；拆解（使某物分解）
分解；腐烂；崩解（自行分解）

senses.title: Split a compound chemically
senses.definition: to separate a compound into simpler substances by chemical action
senses.definitionCN: 通过化学作用把化合物分离成更简单的物质
senses.example: Strong heat decomposes the carbonate into oxide and gas.
senses.exampleCN: 高温把这种碳酸盐分解为氧化物和气体。
senses.why: The verb undoes a combination: de- takes apart what compose had put together.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把「组合」拆掉：de- 把 compose 曾经放在一起的东西分开。

senses.title: Rot away
senses.definition: of dead organic matter, to decay into simpler substances
senses.definitionCN: 指死亡的有机物腐烂成更简单的物质
senses.example: The leaves decompose faster when the soil stays moist.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤保持湿润时，落叶分解得更快。
senses.why: Decay is chemical decomposition happening without a flask, carried out by microbes and water.
senses.whyCN: 腐败就是没有烧瓶的化学分解，由微生物与水来完成。

senses.title: Make something rot
senses.definition: to cause organic material to decay, used with a subject that acts on the object
senses.definitionCN: 使有机材料腐烂，主语对宾语施加作用
senses.example: Bacteria decompose the manure before the field is planted.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌在整地之前把粪肥分解掉。
senses.why: The transitive use adds an agent: someone or something sets the breakdown going.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法增加了施动者：某人或某物让分解开始发生。

senses.title: Split a mathematical object
senses.definition: to express a function, matrix or number as a product or sum of simpler parts
senses.definitionCN: 把函数、矩阵或数表示成更简单部分的乘积或和
senses.example: The program decomposes the matrix before solving the system.
senses.exampleCN: 程序在求解方程组之前先把矩阵分解。
senses.why: Mathematics reuses the verb because the operation is a structured taking-apart, not physical decay.
senses.whyCN: 数学复用这个动词，因为该操作是结构化的拆分，而不是物理腐败。

senses.title: Divide a problem into parts
senses.definition: in computing, to divide a task or system into smaller parts that can be handled separately
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域把任务或系统划分成可分别处理的更小部分
senses.example: We decompose the pipeline into stages that can run in parallel.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把这条流水线拆成可以并行运行的若干阶段。
senses.why: Software work repeats the same gesture at the level of tasks, where the parts are functions rather than molecules.
senses.whyCN: 软件工作在任务层面重复同一动作，只是拆出的部分成了功能而不是分子。

senses.title: Take an argument apart
senses.definition: to analyse a text or argument by separating its claims and assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 通过分离主张与假设来分析文本或论证
senses.example: The class decomposed the editorial into three unsupported claims.
senses.exampleCN: 课堂上把这篇社论拆解成三个缺乏支持的断言。
senses.why: Analytical reading is decomposition in the mind, where the pieces are claims rather than compounds.
senses.whyCN: 分析性阅读是心智中的分解，拆出的碎片是论点而不是化合物。

senses.title: Break down after death
senses.definition: of a body, to pass through the stages of post-mortem breakdown
senses.definitionCN: 指尸体经历死后的各个崩解阶段
senses.example: The body had decomposed for weeks before it was found.
senses.exampleCN: 尸体被发现时已经分解了数周。
senses.why: Forensic writing uses the verb for the whole sequence, keeping the tone clinical rather than emotional.
senses.whyCN: 法医写作使用这个动词描述整个序列，语气保持临床化而非情绪化。

senses.title: Fall apart figuratively
senses.definition: of an organisation, plan or relationship, to disintegrate gradually
senses.definitionCN: 指组织、计划或关系逐渐瓦解
senses.example: The coalition decomposed into rival factions within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个联盟在一年之内瓦解成相互对立的派系。
senses.why: The image of a structure losing its bonds transfers easily to institutions that lose their internal ties.
senses.whyCN: 「结构失去结合」的形象很容易移用到失去内部纽带的机构上。

intro.en: Decompose was formed in French chemistry and then borrowed into English; its Latin parts are de- and componere.
intro.cn: decompose 在法国化学中形成，随后借入英语；其拉丁语成分是 de- 与 componere。

items.en: Compose comes from Latin componere 'to put together', from com- 'together' and ponere 'to place'. The same ponere underlies position, deposit, impose and postpone.
items.cn: compose 来自拉丁语 componere「放在一起」，由 com-「共同」与 ponere「放置」构成。同一个 ponere 也是 position、deposit、impose、postpone 的词根。

items.en: In de- the prefix carries the sense 'apart, away, down', so the new verb means to undo a putting-together.
items.cn: 前缀 de- 带有「分开、离开、向下」之意，因此新动词表示「撤销一次组合」。

items.en: French décomposer is recorded in eighteenth-century chemical writing, when analysts were learning to split compounds into elements. English adopted the verb soon after.
items.cn: 法语 décomposer 见于 18 世纪的化学写作，当时分析家正学着把化合物拆成元素。英语很快借入了这个动词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century biology applied decompose to rotting organisms, giving the everyday sense its scientific footing.
items.cn: 19 世纪的生物学把 decompose 用于腐烂的生物体，使这个日常义项获得科学依据。

items.en: Mathematics and computing later borrowed the verb for structured splitting, while figurative use for failing institutions followed naturally. The first recorded date of each extension is uncertain.
items.cn: 数学与计算随后借用这个动词表示结构化拆分，用于失败机构的比喻用法也自然跟进。各个延伸义项的确切首见年代尚无定论。

note.en: The first group shares the root; the second holds other verbs of breaking down.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根；第二组是其他表示「崩解」的动词。

entries.definition: The process or result; decompose is the action that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或结果；decompose 是产生这一过程的动作。

entries.definition: To put together or create; decompose reverses exactly that direction.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西组合起来或创作；decompose 正是把这一方向反过来。

entries.definition: The organism or device doing the work; it cannot replace the verb in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 执行分解的生物或装置；不能用来替代句中的动词。

entries.definition: To decay naturally, often with a smell; decompose is the neutral term used in science.
entries.definitionCN: 自然腐烂，常带气味；decompose 是科学中的中性说法。

entries.definition: A general phrasal verb for failure or separation, applied to machines and emotions as well as matter.
entries.definitionCN: 通用短语动词，表示故障或分离，可用于机器、情绪与物质。

entries.definition: To break into fragments, often violently or completely; decompose stresses chemical change rather than mechanical shattering.
entries.definitionCN: 碎成小块，常含剧烈或彻底之意；decompose 强调化学变化而非机械碎裂。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the reversal prefix and the verb forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表反转的前缀与动词形式。

normal.en: compose = put together; decompose = take apart.
normal.cn: compose 是放在一起，decompose 是拆开。

normal.en: The forms follow the regular pattern: decomposes, decomposed, decomposing.
normal.cn: 词形变化规律：decomposes、decomposed、decomposing。

normal.en: The object tells you the sense: decompose a compound, a leaf, a matrix, a problem.
normal.cn: 看宾语就能判断义项：分解化合物、落叶、矩阵或问题。

normal.en: The root ponere 'place' links it to position, deposit and impose.
normal.cn: 词根 ponere「放置」把它与 position、deposit、impose 联系起来。

normal.en: The soil under a fallen log is the word's home ground.
normal.cn: 倒木下面的土壤，就是这个词的主场。

abstract.en: Think of a knot loosening thread by thread until the rope is only fibre.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结一根线一根线地松开，直到绳子只剩纤维。

abstract.en: A decomposing log is a book whose pages are being returned to the library of the forest.
abstract.cn: 分解中的倒木是一本书，书页正被还给森林的图书馆。

abstract.en: When a team decomposes a task, it is rotting the workload on purpose.
abstract.cn: 当团队拆分任务时，他们是在有意让工作量「腐烂」掉。

examples.en: Plastic does not decompose easily, which is why it persists in the ocean.
examples.cn: 塑料不易分解，这正是它在海洋中持久存在的原因。

examples.en: The enzyme helps bacteria decompose cellulose in the rumen.
examples.cn: 这种酶帮助细菌分解瘤胃中的纤维素。

examples.en: We decompose the workflow into steps that can be tested separately.
examples.cn: 我们把工作流拆成可以分别测试的步骤。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（拆）+ compose（组成）→ 把组成拆掉 → 分解、腐烂

root: 拉丁语 de-「分开、向下」+ componere「放在一起」（com- + ponere「放置」）；经法语 décomposer 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one action: undoing a structured whole, whether by heat, microbes, mathematics, code, analysis, death or collapse.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：把有结构的整体拆开，手段可以是加热、微生物、数学、代码、分析、死亡或崩解。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bonds loosening until a whole becomes simpler pieces.
core.cn: 核心意象：结合逐渐松开，整体变成更简单的碎片。

branches.en: THE CORE: a compound or a dead body comes apart into simpler substances.
branches.cn: 核心：化合物或尸体拆解为更简单的物质。

branches.en: THE AGENT: a subject can make the breakdown happen, shifting the verb to transitive use.
branches.cn: 施动者：主语可使分解发生，动词由此转为及物用法。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURE: mathematics and computing split objects and tasks by design.
branches.cn: 结构：数学与计算按设计把对象和任务拆开。

branches.en: THE TEXT: an argument is taken apart into claims and assumptions.
branches.cn: 文本：论证被拆成主张与假设。

branches.en: THE END: a body passes through post-mortem stages, and an institution loses its internal bonds.
branches.cn: 终点：尸体经历死后阶段，机构失去内部纽带。

intro.en: Decompose is a reversal prefix on a verb of putting together.
intro.cn: decompose 是在「组合」动词上加表反转的前缀。

latinIntro.en: The elements are de- 'apart' and ponere 'place', the second reached through French composer rather than direct Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 成分是 de-「分开」与 ponere「放置」，后者经法语 composer 而非直接从拉丁语进入。

items.exampleCN: 微生物分解有机层。

items.example: Decomposition releases carbon dioxide.

items.example: A decomposer returns nutrients to the soil.
items.exampleCN: 分解者把养分归还土壤。
