definition_zh: 分解者；分解生物；分解装置
definition_en: an organism or device that breaks dead matter down into simpler substances
core_image: 一撮看不见的菌丝在落叶下面把整片叶子拆成养分
scene: A decomposer such as a soil fungus returns carbon to the air and minerals to the soil.
sceneCN: 这里 decomposer 是「分解者」（第 1 个义项：生态系统中把死亡有机物分解的生物）；句意：土壤真菌这类分解者把碳送回空气，把矿物质归还土壤。

pos.zh: 分解者；分解生物；分解装置（可数，复数 decomposers）

senses.title: The recycler of the ecosystem
senses.definition: an organism, chiefly a bacterium or fungus, that breaks down dead organic matter and releases nutrients
senses.definitionCN: 主要指细菌或真菌，分解死亡有机物并释放养分的生物
senses.example: Fungi and bacteria are the main decomposers in a temperate forest.
senses.exampleCN: 真菌与细菌是温带森林中的主要分解者。
senses.why: Ecology names roles rather than species, and the -er ending marks whatever performs the role of breaking matter down.
senses.whyCN: 生态学命名的是角色而不是物种，-er 词尾标记的是执行「分解物质」这一角色的任何生物。

senses.title: Any organism that breaks matter down
senses.titleCN: 泛指分解有机物的生物
senses.definition: more broadly, any living thing that reduces dead material to simpler forms, including some invertebrates
senses.definitionCN: 更宽泛地指任何把死亡材料还原为更简单形式的生物，包括部分无脊椎动物
senses.example: Woodlice act as decomposers in the first stages of leaf breakdown.
senses.exampleCN: 潮虫在叶片破碎的最初阶段充当分解者。
senses.why: The role is functional, so animals that shred dead matter can share the label with microbes even if their chemistry differs.
senses.whyCN: 这个角色是功能性的，因此即使化学机制不同，撕碎死亡物质的动物也能与微生物共享这一称呼。

senses.title: The microbes in a compost heap
senses.definition: the community of microbes that turns garden or farm waste into compost
senses.definitionCN: 把花园或农场废弃物转化为堆肥的微生物群体
senses.example: A healthy compost heap keeps its decomposers supplied with air and moisture.
senses.exampleCN: 健康的堆肥堆要持续为其中的分解者供应空气与水分。
senses.why: Gardening turns the ecological role into a practical partner, and the plural often names the whole working community.
senses.whyCN: 园艺把这个生态角色变成实际的合作者，复数形式常指整个工作的微生物群体。

senses.title: The cultures in wastewater treatment
senses.titleCN: 污水处理中的分解菌群
senses.definition: the microbial population used in treatment plants to break down organic pollutants
senses.definitionCN: 污水处理厂用来分解有机污染物的微生物种群
senses.example: The plant's decomposers failed when a toxic load arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 有毒负荷到来时，处理厂的分解菌群失效了。
senses.why: Engineering recruits the same organisms as workers, so the word becomes the name of a managed culture.
senses.whyCN: 工程把这些生物招募为工人，这个词因此成为一种被管理的菌群的名称。

senses.title: An industrial breakdown unit
senses.definition: a machine or vessel that breaks organic waste down under controlled conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在受控条件下分解有机废弃物的机器或容器
senses.example: The hotel installed an on-site decomposer for food waste.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店就地安装了一台厨余分解装置。
senses.why: Once the process is mechanized, the agent noun can name the machine that does what microbes do.
senses.whyCN: 一旦过程机械化，这个施动名词就能指代做微生物工作的机器。

senses.title: A chemical breakdown agent
senses.definition: a substance or reagent that causes another compound to break apart
senses.definitionCN: 使另一种化合物分解的物质或试剂
senses.example: The lab added a chemical decomposer to the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室向样品中加入了一种化学分解剂。
senses.why: Chemistry applies the -er agent pattern to reagents, where the actor is a substance rather than an organism.
senses.whyCN: 化学把 -er 的施动模式用在试剂上，施动者成了物质而不是生物。

senses.title: One who takes a problem apart
senses.definition: figuratively, a person or method that separates a complex whole into manageable parts
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指把复杂整体拆成可处理部分的人或方法
senses.example: She is the team's decomposer, turning vague goals into concrete tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 她是团队里的拆解者，把模糊目标变成具体任务。
senses.why: The analytic sense keeps the literal structure: a whole is reduced to parts so that each can be handled.
senses.whyCN: 分析义保持了字面结构：整体被还原为部分，以便逐一处理。

senses.title: One who clears up a mess
senses.definition: figuratively, a person who deals with the remains of a failed project or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指处理失败项目或争端遗留残局的人
senses.example: After the merger collapsed, a small team of decomposers settled the contracts.
senses.exampleCN: 合并失败后，一个负责收拾残局的小组处理了合同事宜。
senses.why: The word borrows the ecological image of turning remains into something usable, applied to institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这个词借用了生态学「把残余转化为可用之物」的形象，用在机构情境中。

intro.en: Decomposer is an English agent noun: the verb decompose plus -er.
intro.cn: decomposer 是英语的施动名词：动词 decompose 加 -er。

items.en: Decompose came into English from French décomposer, built on Latin de- 'apart' and componere 'to put together'.
items.cn: decompose 经法语 décomposer 进入英语，其基础是拉丁语 de-「分开」与 componere「放在一起」。

items.en: The English suffix -er forms agent nouns from verbs, as in builder and worker; it has no Latin origin here, though it is distantly related to Latin -arius.
items.cn: 英语后缀 -er 由动词构成施动名词，如 builder、worker；此处它并非拉丁来源，尽管与拉丁语 -arius 有远亲关系。

items.en: Nineteenth-century chemistry used decomposer for reagents and agents that cause breakdown, following the new French chemical vocabulary.
items.cn: 19 世纪的化学沿用法国化学新词，用 decomposer 指引起分解的试剂与动因。

items.en: In the twentieth century, ecology made decomposer a standard term for bacteria and fungi that mineralize dead matter. The exact first use in this sense is not firmly established.
items.cn: 20 世纪，生态学把 decomposer 变成细菌与真菌的标准称谓，指把死亡物质矿化的生物。这一义项的确切首见出处尚无定论。

items.en: Late twentieth-century waste management extended the word to composting machines and anaerobic digesters.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期的废弃物管理把这个词扩展到堆肥机与厌氧消化器。

note.en: The first group is the same word family; the second holds other ecological roles.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族；第二组是其他生态角色。

entries.definition: The action of breaking down; a decomposer is what carries it out.
entries.definitionCN: 指分解动作；decomposer 是实施这一动作的主体。

entries.definition: The process itself; decomposers are the agents that drive it.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程本身；decomposers 是推动这一过程的动因。

entries.definition: Describes material that can be broken down; it says nothing about who does it.
entries.definitionCN: 描述可被分解的材料，不说明由谁完成分解。

entries.definition: An animal that ingests dead fragments; a decomposer often absorbs dissolved products rather than eating particles.
entries.definitionCN: 摄入死亡碎片的动物；分解者常吸收溶解产物，而不是吞食颗粒。

entries.definition: An animal that feeds on dead bodies; it removes remains, while a decomposer transforms them chemically.
entries.definitionCN: 以尸体为食的动物；它移走残余，而分解者在化学上转化残余。

entries.definition: The formal ecological term for an organism absorbing nutrients from dead matter, especially fungi.
entries.definitionCN: 指从死亡物质吸收养分的生物的正式生态学术语，尤指真菌。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the agent ending and the ecological role.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：施动词尾与生态角色。

normal.en: decompose + -er: the one that does the decomposing.
normal.cn: decompose + -er：执行分解的那一方。

normal.en: Microbes, compost heaps, treatment plants and machines can all be decomposers.
normal.cn: 微生物、堆肥堆、处理厂与机器都可以是 decomposer。

normal.en: The phrase decomposer community treats the role as a group, not an individual.
normal.cn: decomposer community 这个说法把角色视为一个群体，而不是个体。

normal.en: The formal synonym saprotroph is useful when precision matters.
normal.cn: 需要精确时，正式同义词 saprotroph 很有用。

normal.en: The root ponere 'place' hides inside, linking it to composition and position.
normal.cn: 词根 ponere「放置」藏在其中，把它与 composition、position 连起来。

abstract.en: Think of a night-shift crew that never appears in the photographs but keeps the city running.
abstract.cn: 想象一支从不出现在照片里、却让城市继续运转的夜班队伍。

abstract.en: A decomposer is the forest's accountant: it closes every account that life leaves open.
abstract.cn: 分解者是森林的会计：生命留下的每一笔账都由它结清。

abstract.en: In a team, the decomposer is the person who splits an impossible goal into next steps.
abstract.cn: 在团队里，decomposer 就是把不可能的目标拆成下一步行动的人。

examples.en: Without decomposers, dead trees would pile up faster than they could fall.
examples.cn: 没有分解者，死树堆积的速度会超过它们倒下的速度。

examples.en: The compost needs a balance of decomposers, air and moisture.
examples.cn: 堆肥需要分解者、空气与水分的平衡。

examples.en: She acted as the decomposer of a plan everyone else found too large.
examples.cn: 大家都觉得计划太庞大时，她充当了拆解它的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: decompose（分解）+ er（做的人/物）→ 分解者

root: decompose（拉丁语 de-「分开」+ componere「放在一起」；经法语进入英语）+ 英语施动后缀 -er → decomposer「执行分解者」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one role: the agent that reduces a whole to parts. The agent may be a fungus, a microbial community, a machine, a reagent or a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项保持同一个角色：把整体还原为部分的动因。这个动因可以是真菌、微生物群落、机器、试剂或人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unseen worker turning remains into raw material.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个看不见的工人把残余变成原料。

branches.en: THE CORE: any organism that reduces dead matter can be called a decomposer, whatever its size.
branches.cn: 核心：任何把死亡物质还原的生物都可称为分解者，无论体型大小。

branches.en: THE COMMUNITY: gardening and wastewater treatment manage whole populations of decomposers.
branches.cn: 群体：园艺与污水处理管理的是整个分解者种群。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: industry copies the biological role in a vessel.
branches.cn: 机器：工业在容器中复制这一生物角色。

branches.en: THE REAGENT: chemistry applies the agent noun to substances that cause breakdown.
branches.cn: 试剂：化学把施动名词用在引起分解的物质上。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the same image serves for analysts who split problems and fixers who clear up remains.
branches.cn: 人：同一形象也适用于拆分问题的分析者与收拾残局的善后者。

intro.en: Decomposer is a verb plus the English agent ending -er.
intro.cn: decomposer 是动词加英语施动词尾 -er。

latinIntro.en: The Latin part lies inside the verb: de- 'apart' and ponere 'place'. The -er ending is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语部分在动词内部：de-「分开」与 ponere「放置」。词尾 -er 是英语本族成分。

items.meaning: the agent that breaks matter down
items.example: The decomposer releases nitrogen into the soil.
items.exampleCN: 分解者把氮释放到土壤中。

items.example: The fungus decomposes dead wood.
items.exampleCN: 这种真菌分解枯木。

items.example: Decomposition is slow in cold water.
items.exampleCN: 冷水中的分解很慢。

items.example: The bag is decomposable in industrial compost.
items.exampleCN: 这种袋子在工业堆肥中可分解。

items.example: These cells compose the fungal mat.
items.exampleCN: 这些细胞构成了真菌垫。

items.example: The decomposer's position in the food web is low.
items.exampleCN: 分解者在食物网中的位置较低。

items.example: Decomposers prevent deposits of undecayed litter.
items.exampleCN: 分解者可防止未分解枯落物堆积。

items.meaning: decayed organic material used as fertilizer
items.meaningCN: 用作肥料的腐熟有机物
items.example: The compost is the work of many decomposers.
items.exampleCN: 这堆堆肥是许多分解者的成果。

definition_zh: 可分解的；可降解的；可拆解的
definition_en: capable of being broken down into simpler parts
core_image: 一只纸袋埋在土里，几个月后只剩纤维的痕迹
scene: The packaging is fully decomposable, so it can be buried with the food waste.
sceneCN: 这里 decomposable 是「可降解的」（第 2 个义项：可被微生物降解）；句意：这种包装可完全降解，因此可以和厨余一起埋掉。

pos.zh: 可分解的；可降解的；可拆解的

senses.title: Able to be split chemically
senses.definition: describing a compound that can be separated into simpler substances
senses.definitionCN: 描述可被分离成更简单物质的化合物
senses.example: The solvent is decomposable at high temperature into two gases.
senses.exampleCN: 这种溶剂在高温下可分解为两种气体。
senses.why: The suffix -able adds possibility to the verb, so the adjective says the breakdown can happen rather than that it has happened.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 给动词加上「可能」，因此形容词说的是分解「可以发生」，而不是已经发生。

senses.title: Able to be biodegraded
senses.definition: describing material that microbes can break down within a reasonable time
senses.definitionCN: 描述微生物能在合理时间内分解的材料
senses.example: The bag is decomposable in a home compost bin.
senses.exampleCN: 这种袋子在家庭堆肥桶中可降解。
senses.why: Environmental writing uses the adjective for materials designed to disappear through microbial action.
senses.whyCN: 环保写作使用这个形容词来描述被设计成可通过微生物作用消失的材料。

senses.title: Able to rot away
senses.definition: describing dead organic matter that will decay naturally
senses.definitionCN: 描述会自然腐烂的死亡有机物
senses.example: All the garden waste here is decomposable within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这里所有的花园废弃物都能在一年内腐烂。
senses.why: The adjective generalizes the chemistry of decay to any organic material, without naming the microbes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把腐烂的化学过程泛化到任何有机材料，而不点名微生物。

senses.title: Able to be taken apart
senses.definition: describing a structure or device whose parts can be separated
senses.definitionCN: 描述其部件可被分离的结构或装置
senses.example: The shelter is decomposable into panels one person can carry.
senses.exampleCN: 这座棚屋可拆解成一个人能搬运的板材。
senses.why: Mechanical use extends the same possibility from molecules to parts, where separation is physical rather than chemical.
senses.whyCN: 机械义项把同样的「可能性」从分子扩展到部件，分离成了物理过程而非化学过程。

senses.title: Able to be factored
senses.definition: describing a mathematical object that can be expressed as a product or sum of simpler objects
senses.definitionCN: 描述可表示成更简单对象之乘积或和的数学对象
senses.example: The matrix is decomposable into two triangular factors.
senses.exampleCN: 这个矩阵可分解为两个三角因子。
senses.why: Mathematics borrows the adjective for objects whose structure permits a standard split.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用这个形容词描述结构上允许标准拆分的对象。

senses.title: Able to be modularised
senses.definition: in computing, describing a system that can be divided into independent modules
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域描述可划分为独立模块的系统
senses.example: The old monolith is not easily decomposable into services.
senses.exampleCN: 这个旧单体系统不容易拆分成若干服务。
senses.why: Software architecture treats decomposability as a design property, so the adjective judges systems rather than substances.
senses.whyCN: 软件架构把「可分解性」当作设计属性，因此这个形容词评判的是系统而不是物质。

senses.title: Suitable for composting
senses.definition: describing waste that a composting system can accept and process
senses.definitionCN: 描述堆肥系统可以接收并处理的废弃物
senses.example: Only decomposable cutlery is allowed at the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 节日上只允许使用可堆肥处理的餐具。
senses.why: Waste management narrows the general property to what a particular facility can actually process.
senses.whyCN: 废弃物管理把这一泛化属性收窄为「某套设施实际能处理」的范围。

senses.title: Able to be analysed apart
senses.definition: figuratively, describing a complex idea or institution that can be separated into understandable parts
senses.definitionCN: 比喻描述可拆成可理解部分的复杂观念或机构
senses.example: The problem is decomposable into three decisions, not one big one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题可以拆成三个决定，而不是一个大决定。
senses.why: The analytic sense treats understanding as a form of breakdown, keeping the parts-and-whole structure.
senses.whyCN: 分析义把理解视为一种分解，仍保留「部分与整体」的结构。

intro.en: Decomposable is decompose plus the Latin-derived English ending -able.
intro.cn: decomposable 是 decompose 加上源自拉丁语的英语词尾 -able。

items.en: The suffix -able continues Latin -abilis, 'capable of being', built on the verb stem plus -bilis. It entered English through French -able.
items.cn: 后缀 -able 承自拉丁语 -abilis「能够被……的」，由动词词干加 -bilis 构成，经法语 -able 进入英语。

items.en: Decompose itself came from French décomposer, built on de- and componere 'to put together'.
items.cn: decompose 本身来自法语 décomposer，建立在 de- 与 componere「放在一起」之上。

items.en: Nineteenth-century chemistry needed adjectives for substances that could be separated, and decomposable joined a large family of -able technical terms.
items.cn: 19 世纪的化学需要形容词来描述可被分离的物质，decomposable 加入了庞大的 -able 技术术语家族。

items.en: Late twentieth-century packaging and waste debates made decomposable a common label for biodegradable products. The exact first use in advertising is not documented here.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期的包装与废弃物争论使 decomposable 成为可降解产品的常见标签。广告中的确切首用此处不作断言。

items.en: Mathematics and software engineering later applied the adjective to objects and systems whose structure allows a clean split.
items.cn: 数学与软件工程随后把这个形容词用于结构上允许干净拆分的对象与系统。

note.en: The first group is the same family in other forms; the second holds related material labels.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族的其他形式；第二组是相关的材料标签。

entries.definition: The action; decomposable describes the capacity, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指动作；decomposable 描述能力，而不是动作。

entries.definition: The process itself; decomposable says the process can occur.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程本身；decomposable 说明该过程可以发生。

entries.definition: The organism or device that does it; the adjective never names an agent.
entries.definitionCN: 执行分解的生物或装置；形容词不指施动者。

entries.definition: Breakable down by living organisms; decomposable is broader because it can also mean chemical or mechanical separation.
entries.definitionCN: 可被生物分解的；decomposable 范围更宽，还可指化学或机械分离。

entries.definition: Able to break down in a composting system to usable soil; stricter than decomposable.
entries.definitionCN: 可在堆肥系统中分解为可用土壤；比 decomposable 要求更严。

entries.definition: Designed to be thrown away after use; it says nothing about whether the item will break down.
entries.definitionCN: 设计为用后即弃；并不说明该物品是否会分解。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: -able as possibility and the material labels.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：-able 表示可能性，以及相关的材料标签。

normal.en: -able = can be: decompose + able = can be decomposed.
normal.cn: -able 表示「可以被」：decompose + able = 可以被分解。

normal.en: The word joins a family: biodegradable, compostable, recyclable.
normal.cn: 这个词属于一个家族：biodegradable、compostable、recyclable。

normal.en: The ordinary phrase is fully decomposable, common on packaging.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 fully decomposable，常见于包装标识。

normal.en: The noun decomposability names the property itself.
normal.cn: 名词 decomposability 指这种性质本身。

normal.en: The same adjective works for a compound, a bag, a panel, a matrix or a plan.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词可用于化合物、袋子、板材、矩阵或计划。

abstract.en: Think of a sugar cube in tea: the question is not whether it is sweet but whether it can disappear.
abstract.cn: 想象茶里的方糖：问题不是它甜不甜，而是它能不能消失。

abstract.en: A decomposable plan is one that can be reduced to steps small enough to start.
abstract.cn: 可拆解的计划，就是能缩小到足以立刻开始的若干步骤的计划。

abstract.en: Packaging that says decomposable is making a promise about time, not about material.
abstract.cn: 标注可分解的包装，承诺的是时间，而不是材料。

examples.en: The new trays are decomposable in commercial compost.
examples.cn: 这种新托盘在商业堆肥中可分解。

examples.en: Not every plastic labelled decomposable breaks down in seawater.
examples.cn: 并非所有标为可分解的塑料都能在海水中降解。

examples.en: The model is decomposable into two independent modules.
examples.cn: 这个模型可拆分为两个独立模块。

dict_mnemonic.text: decompose（分解）+ able（能……的）→ 能分解的 → 可降解的

root: decompose（拉丁语 de-「分开」+ componere「放在一起」；经法语进入英语）+ 拉丁语 -abilis「能够被……的」（英语 -able）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all state a capacity: a compound, a material, dead matter, a structure, a matrix, a system, waste and an idea can each be taken apart.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在陈述一种能力：化合物、材料、死亡物质、结构、矩阵、系统、废弃物与观念都可以被拆开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole that is able to come apart when the right force is applied.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个在施加合适力量时能够散开的整体。

branches.en: THE CORE: possibility is attached to a compound or to dead matter that will decay.
branches.cn: 核心：可能性附着在化合物或终将腐烂的死亡物质上。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL LABEL: microbiology and waste management ask what a facility can actually process.
branches.cn: 材料标签：微生物学与废弃物管理关心的是设施实际能处理什么。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a built thing can be separated into parts by hand.
branches.cn: 实物：人造物可以被手工拆成部件。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURE: matrices and software systems are judged by whether they admit a clean split.
branches.cn: 结构：矩阵与软件系统按「是否允许干净拆分」来评判。

branches.en: THE IDEA: a complex problem is decomposable into decisions small enough to take.
branches.cn: 观念：复杂问题可以拆成小到足以做出的决定。

intro.en: Decomposable is a verb base plus a suffix of possibility.
intro.cn: decomposable 是动词词基加表示可能性的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies de- 'apart', ponere 'place' and -abilis 'able to be'; the -able ending reached English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 de-「分开」、ponere「放置」与 -abilis「能够被……」，其中 -able 经法语进入英语。

items.example: The film is decomposable in soil.
items.exampleCN: 这种薄膜在土壤中可分解。

items.example: Heat decomposes the compound.
items.exampleCN: 加热分解这种化合物。

items.example: Decomposition takes longer in dry soil.
items.exampleCN: 干燥土壤中的分解更慢。

items.example: A decomposer consumes the dead leaves.
items.exampleCN: 分解者消耗掉死叶。

items.example: Biodegradable is narrower than decomposable.
items.exampleCN: biodegradable 比 decomposable 范围更窄。

items.example: The label says compostable, not merely decomposable.
items.exampleCN: 标签写的是「可堆肥」，而不仅是「可分解」。

items.meaning: able to be processed and reused
items.example: Recyclable and decomposable are different claims.
items.exampleCN: 「可回收」与「可分解」是两种不同的宣称。

items.meaning: able to last, the opposite capacity
items.meaningCN: 能持久的，是相反的能力
items.example: Durable goods resist the breakdown that decomposable ones allow.
items.exampleCN: 耐用品抵抗分解，而可分解物品允许分解。

definition_en: loose fragments of dead or broken material
core_image: 河湾浅水处堆积着碎叶、贝壳和细沙
scene: The stream slows here, and detritus settles into a thick layer of leaf fragments.
sceneCN: 这里 detritus 是「腐屑、碎屑」（第 2 个义项：生态学中有机碎屑）；句意：溪水在这里变缓，碎屑沉积成厚厚一层叶片残片。

pos.zh: 碎屑；腐屑；岩屑；残骸（不可数）

senses.title: Rock fragments
senses.definition: in geology, loose broken rock material produced by weathering
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中由风化作用产生的松散岩石碎块
senses.example: Detritus from the cliff feeds the beach below.
senses.exampleCN: 悬崖上落下的岩屑为下方的海滩提供沉积物。
senses.why: Geology uses the oldest technical sense: material worn or rubbed off a larger body.
senses.whyCN: 地质学使用的是最古老的技术义项：从更大物体上被磨损、摩擦下来的材料。

senses.title: Dead organic fragments
senses.definition: in ecology, the dead plant and animal fragments that accumulate in soil or water
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中积聚在土壤或水体中的死亡动植物碎片
senses.example: Detritus on the river bed supports a dense community of invertebrates.
senses.exampleCN: 河床上的腐屑支撑着密集的无脊椎动物群落。
senses.why: The geological image transfers to organic remains: what is broken off is now dead tissue rather than rock.
senses.whyCN: 地质形象移用到有机物上：被拆散下来的不再是岩石，而是死亡组织。

senses.title: Rubble and wreckage
senses.definition: loose debris left by construction, demolition or war
senses.definitionCN: 施工、拆除或战争留下的松散废弃物
senses.example: Detritus from the collapsed wall blocked the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 倒塌墙体留下的瓦砾堵住了小巷。
senses.why: Human demolition produces the same kind of loose fragments, so the word moves easily from cliffs to cities.
senses.whyCN: 人类拆建会产生同样的松散碎块，因此这个词从悬崖轻易移到了城市。

senses.title: Remains of a body
senses.definition: in forensic or archaeological contexts, the scattered remains of a decomposed body
senses.definitionCN: 法医或考古语境中分解尸体散落的残骸
senses.example: Investigators recovered bone detritus from the shallow grave.
senses.exampleCN: 调查人员从浅坑中取回了骨骼残骸。
senses.why: A body that has broken down leaves fragments, and the neutral noun avoids the emotional weight of corpse.
senses.whyCN: 分解后的尸体会留下碎片，这个中性名词避开了 corpse 的情绪重量。

senses.title: Sinking particles
senses.definition: in oceanography, organic particles sinking from surface waters, often called marine snow
senses.definitionCN: 海洋学中从表层水域下沉的有机颗粒，常称「海洋雪」
senses.example: Deep-sea detritus supplies food to communities far below the sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 深海碎屑为远离阳光的群落提供食物。
senses.why: Open-ocean ecology extends the term to particles in transit, because they are fragments of dead matter falling through water.
senses.whyCN: 开阔海洋生态学把这个词扩展到沉降中的颗粒，因为它们也是穿过水体下沉的死亡物质碎片。

senses.title: Soil's mineral crumbs
senses.definition: in soil science, the mineral grains and rock fragments that form part of the parent material
senses.definitionCN: 土壤学中构成母质一部分的矿物颗粒与岩石碎片
senses.example: The soil's detritus comes mostly from weathered granite.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土壤的矿物碎屑主要来自风化的花岗岩。
senses.why: Soil science keeps the geological sense alive inside the profile, where fragments are not yet soil.
senses.whyCN: 土壤学在剖面中保留了地质义项，那里的碎块尚未变成土壤。

senses.title: Leftovers of an idea or culture
senses.definition: figuratively, the small remnants of a system, tradition or idea that survive after its decline
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指体系、传统或观念衰落后仍存留的细小残余
senses.example: The essay traces the detritus of an older philosophy in modern policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章在现代政策中追寻一种旧哲学的残余。
senses.why: The metaphor follows the literal sense: what remains of a larger thing is small, scattered and no longer whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻沿用了字面义：更大事物留下的东西是细小的、散落的、不再完整。

senses.title: Stone chips in an excavation
senses.definition: in archaeology, the small stone chips and flakes left by tool-making or building
senses.definitionCN: 考古学中制作工具或营建活动留下的碎石片
senses.example: The floor layer held detritus from flint knapping.
senses.exampleCN: 地面层中留有打制燧石产生的石屑。
senses.why: Archaeology reads behaviour from the small fragments left behind, so the word names evidence rather than waste.
senses.whyCN: 考古学从留下的小碎片读出行为，因此这个词指证据，而不是垃圾。

intro.en: Detritus is a Latin past participle used as a noun: 'that which has been rubbed away'.
intro.cn: detritus 是一个作名词用的拉丁语过去分词，意为「被磨掉的东西」。

items.en: Latin deterere means 'to rub away, wear down'. It joins de- 'away' and terere 'to rub', the same verb behind trite and attrition.
items.cn: 拉丁语 deterere 意为「磨掉、磨蚀」，由 de-「离开」与 terere「摩擦」构成；trite 与 attrition 也出自同一个动词。

items.en: The neuter past participle detritum, used as a noun, is Latin detritus. English borrowed the form directly, keeping its Latin look.
items.cn: 中性过去分词 detritum 用作名词即拉丁语 detritus。英语直接借用了这一形式，保留了它的拉丁语外观。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology adopted detritus for loose weathered rock, when sedimentary processes were being described systematically. The precise first use is not certain.
items.cn: 19 世纪地质学在系统描述沉积过程时，采用 detritus 指松散的风化岩石。确切首见出处并不确定。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology extended the word to organic fragments in soil, rivers and the sea, giving rise to the detritus food chain.
items.cn: 20 世纪生态学把这个词扩展到土壤、河流与海洋中的有机碎片，并由此产生「碎屑食物链」的说法。

items.en: Forensic and archaeological writing later used detritus for scattered remains and tool-making chips, where fragments are read as evidence.
items.cn: 法医与考古写作随后用 detritus 指散落的残骸与制石碎片，此时碎片被当作证据来解读。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root or looks close; the second holds near-synonyms for fragments.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根或形近；第二组是表示碎片的近义词。

entries.definition: Describing material made of detritus, as in detrital rock; the noun names the material itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述由碎屑构成的材料，如碎屑岩；名词本身指材料。

entries.definition: An animal that feeds on detritus; it is the consumer, not the fragments.
entries.definitionCN: 以碎屑为食的动物；它是取食者，不是碎屑本身。

entries.definition: Harm or damage, from Latin detrimentum, 'a wearing away'; it shares deterere with detritus but long ago left the physical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 损害、伤害，来自拉丁语 detrimentum「磨损」；与 detritus 共享 deterere，但早已离开物理义。

entries.definition: Scattered fragments of destroyed material, borrowed from French; detritus is more technical and includes organic fragments.
entries.definitionCN: 被毁材料散落的碎片，借自法语；detritus 更技术化，且包含有机碎片。

entries.definition: Material that has settled to the bottom of water or been laid down; detritus may be suspended before it becomes sediment.
entries.definitionCN: 沉降到水底或被铺设下来的材料；detritus 在成为沉积物之前可能仍悬浮。

entries.definition: Large irregular pieces of broken stone or brick; detritus usually means finer fragments.
entries.definitionCN: 破碎石头或砖块的大而不规则的块体；detritus 通常指更细的碎片。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin rubbing image and the scientific collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语「摩擦」意象与科学搭配。

normal.en: Latin deterere 'rub away' gives detritus, detrition and detriment.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 deterere「磨掉」产生 detritus、detrition、detriment。

normal.en: The collocations mark the fields: organic detritus, leaf detritus, detritus food chain.
normal.cn: 搭配标出领域：有机碎屑、叶片碎屑、碎屑食物链。

normal.en: The adjective is detrital, the eater is a detritivore.
normal.cn: 形容词是 detrital，取食者是 detritivore。

normal.en: Detritus is uncountable: you speak of a layer of detritus, not of detrituses.
normal.cn: detritus 不可数：说 a layer of detritus，而不说 detrituses。

normal.en: The river bend with its mat of leaves is the word's clearest scene.
normal.cn: 河湾里那层叶片垫，是这个词最清楚的场景。

abstract.en: Think of a cliff's slow donation to the beach: every grain was once part of something larger.
abstract.cn: 想象悬崖缓慢地馈赠海滩：每一粒都曾是更大事物的一部分。

abstract.en: A culture's detritus is what survives when the building is gone: habits, phrases, small rituals.
abstract.cn: 一种文化的残余是建筑消失后仍留下的东西：习惯、说法、小小的仪式。

abstract.en: Marine snow is detritus falling like slow weather through dark water.
abstract.cn: 海洋雪就是碎屑像缓慢的天气一样落过黑暗水体。

examples.en: Organic detritus in the soil feeds the decomposers below it.
examples.cn: 土壤中的有机碎屑供养其下方的分解者。

examples.en: The flood left a layer of detritus across the field.
examples.cn: 洪水在田野上留下一层碎屑。

examples.en: Archaeologists sifted the detritus for clues about tool-making.
examples.cn: 考古学家筛检这些碎屑，寻找关于制石工具的线索。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（掉）+ tri（碎）+ tus → 掉下来的碎东西 → 碎屑、腐屑

root: 拉丁语 detritus，为 deterere「磨掉、磨蚀」的过去分词（de-「离开」+ terere「摩擦」）→ 字面「被磨掉的东西」→ 碎屑、腐屑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe fragments separated from something larger: rock, dead tissue, buildings, bodies, sinking particles, soil grains, ideas and stone chips.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述从更大事物上分离出来的碎片：岩石、死亡组织、建筑、尸体、沉降颗粒、土壤颗粒、观念与石屑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small pieces that were once part of a larger whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：曾是更大整体一部分的小碎片。

branches.en: THE MINERAL: weathering breaks rock into fragments that later become sediment or soil parent material.
branches.cn: 矿物：风化把岩石打碎成碎片，这些碎片后来成为沉积物或土壤母质。

branches.en: THE ORGANIC: dead tissue becomes detritus on land, in rivers and in the deep sea.
branches.cn: 有机：死亡组织在陆地、河流与深海中都成为碎屑。

branches.en: THE RUIN: demolition and war leave the same kind of loose fragments at human scale.
branches.cn: 废墟：拆建与战争在人类尺度上留下同类松散碎片。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE: scattered body remains and knapping chips are read as traces of past events.
branches.cn: 证据：散落的遗体残骸与打石碎片被读作往昔事件的痕迹。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: ideas also leave small remains after the larger system declines.
branches.cn: 隐喻：更大的体系衰落后，观念同样会留下细小残余。

intro.en: Detritus is a Latin participle form, not an English compound.
intro.cn: detritus 是拉丁语分词形式，不是英语复合词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin terere 'to rub', behind detritus, detrition, trite and attrition, with the prefix de- 'away'.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 terere「摩擦」，detritus、detrition、trite、attrition 都出自它，并带前缀 de-「离开」。

items.example: Detritus carpets the slow part of the stream.
items.exampleCN: 碎屑铺满溪流流速较缓的地段。

items.meaning: made of or relating to detritus
items.meaningCN: 由碎屑构成或与碎屑有关的
items.example: Detrital rock forms from compressed fragments.
items.exampleCN: 碎屑岩由压实的碎片形成。

items.example: The detritivore feeds on the leaf mat.
items.exampleCN: 这种食碎屑动物取食叶片垫。

items.example: Detritivorous fish graze the bottom.
items.exampleCN: 食碎屑鱼类在底部觅食。

items.example: Detrition shapes the pebbles over centuries.
items.exampleCN: 磨蚀在数百年间塑造了这些卵石。

items.meaningCN: 因过度使用而磨损，故指陈腐的
items.example: Trite and detritus share the idea of rubbing.
items.exampleCN: trite 与 detritus 共享「摩擦」这一概念。

items.example: Attrition reduces the fragments to sand.
items.exampleCN: 磨耗把这些碎片变成沙子。

items.example: Debris is not related to detritus by root.
items.exampleCN: debris 与 detritus 在词根上并无亲缘关系。

latinEntries.structure: past participle of deterere, used as a noun
latinEntries.meaning: that which has been rubbed away

definition_zh: 食碎屑动物；以腐屑为食的动物
definition_en: an animal that feeds on detritus, the dead and broken fragments of other organisms
core_image: 一只小虾在河底把烂叶碎片一点点送进嘴里
scene: The mayfly larva is a detritivore that shreds leaf litter at the bottom of the stream.
sceneCN: 这里 detritivore 是「食碎屑动物」（第 1 个义项：以腐屑为食的动物）；句意：蜉蝣幼虫是食碎屑动物，在溪流底部把落叶撕碎取食。

pos.zh: 食碎屑动物；食腐屑生物（可数，复数 detritivores）

senses.title: An animal living on detritus
senses.definition: an animal whose main food is dead, fragmented organic matter
senses.definitionCN: 以死亡、破碎的有机物为主要食物的动物
senses.example: Earthworms are detritivores that process enormous amounts of soil.
senses.exampleCN: 蚯蚓是食碎屑动物，处理大量土壤。
senses.why: The word combines the name of the food with the -vore ending for eaters, so the diet itself defines the animal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把食物的名称与表示取食者的 -vore 词尾结合，因此食性本身就定义了这种动物。

senses.title: A bottom-dwelling shredder
senses.definition: an aquatic animal that shreds and eats leaf litter and other coarse detritus on the bottom
senses.definitionCN: 在水底撕碎并取食落叶等粗大腐屑的水生动物
senses.example: Caddis larvae are detritivores that break leaves into finer particles.
senses.exampleCN: 石蛾幼虫是食碎屑动物，把叶片破碎成更细的颗粒。
senses.why: Stream ecology focuses on the mechanical act of shredding, because it converts coarse litter into food others can use.
senses.whyCN: 溪流生态学关注「撕碎」这一机械动作，因为它把粗大枯落物变成其他生物可用的食物。

senses.title: A soil worker
senses.definition: a soil animal that feeds on dead plant material and mixes it into the soil
senses.definitionCN: 取食死亡植物材料并将其混入土壤的土壤动物
senses.example: The soil detritivore population doubled after the leaf fall.
senses.exampleCN: 落叶之后，土壤食碎屑动物的数量翻了一番。
senses.why: Soil biology highlights the mixing effect: feeding on fragments is also a way of building soil structure.
senses.whyCN: 土壤生物学强调混合作用：取食碎片同时也是构建土壤结构的方式。

senses.title: A member of a feeding guild
senses.definition: an organism classified in the detritus food chain by its feeding role
senses.definitionCN: 按取食角色被归入碎屑食物链的生物
senses.example: The study grouped detritivores, grazers and predators by guild.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究按功能群把食碎屑者、刮食者与捕食者分组。
senses.why: Ecology classifies by function, so any animal that eats detritus joins the same guild regardless of taxonomy.
senses.whyCN: 生态学按功能分类，因此任何吃碎屑的动物都归入同一功能群，无论分类地位如何。

senses.title: The partner of decomposers
senses.titleCN: 与分解者分工的取食者
senses.definition: an animal that reduces particle size so microbes can complete chemical breakdown
senses.definitionCN: 通过减小颗粒尺寸，使微生物得以完成化学分解的动物
senses.example: Detritivores and decomposers together return the forest's nutrients.
senses.exampleCN: 食碎屑动物与分解者共同归还森林的养分。
senses.why: The distinction is functional: animals chew and fragment, microbes mineralize, and the two steps complement each other.
senses.whyCN: 这一区分是功能性的：动物咀嚼破碎，微生物矿化，两个步骤彼此补足。

senses.title: A named taxonomic example
senses.definition: a specific group such as isopods, amphipods or dipteran larvae known for detritus feeding
senses.definitionCN: 等足类、端足类或双翅目幼虫等以食碎屑著称的具体类群
senses.example: Amphipods are common detritivores in cold coastal waters.
senses.exampleCN: 端足类是寒冷沿海水域常见的食碎屑动物。
senses.why: Field guides need a label for whole groups whose members share the habit, so the ecological term doubles as a descriptive tag.
senses.whyCN: 野外手册需要给习性相同的整个类群一个标签，因此这个生态学术语也兼作描述性标签。

senses.title: A user of waste in aquaculture
senses.definition: in aquaculture, an animal used to consume leftover feed and organic waste
senses.definitionCN: 水产养殖中用来消耗残饵与有机废弃物的动物
senses.example: The farm added detritivores to clean the pond bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 养殖场加入食碎屑动物来清理池底。
senses.why: Applied ecology turns the feeding habit into a service, and the word names the worker rather than the wild animal.
senses.whyCN: 应用生态学把这种食性变成服务，这个词指的就是「工人」，而不是野生个体。

senses.title: An eater in the fossil record
senses.titleCN: 化石记录中的食碎屑者
senses.definition: a fossil animal inferred to have fed on detritus from its mouthparts or gut contents
senses.definitionCN: 依据口器或肠道内容物推断以碎屑为食的化石动物
senses.example: The trace fossils suggest detritivores worked the ancient sea floor.
senses.exampleCN: 这些遗迹化石表明食碎屑动物曾在古代海底活动。
senses.why: Paleoecology reconstructs feeding from preserved traces, so the term describes an inferred role rather than an observed one.
senses.whyCN: 古生态学从保存下来的痕迹重建取食行为，因此这个词描述的是推断出的角色，而不是观察到的角色。

intro.en: Detritivore is a twentieth-century scientific compound: detritus plus the -vore ending for eaters.
intro.cn: detritivore 是 20 世纪的科学复合词：detritus 加上表示取食者的 -vore 词尾。

items.en: Detritus is the past participle of Latin deterere, 'to rub away' (de- 'away' + terere 'to rub'). It names material worn off a larger body.
items.cn: detritus 是拉丁语 deterere「磨掉」的过去分词（de-「离开」+ terere「摩擦」），指从更大物体上磨下来的材料。

items.en: The -vore ending comes from Latin vorare, 'to devour', the same root as voracious and carnivore.
items.cn: -vore 词尾来自拉丁语 vorare「吞食」，与 voracious、carnivore 同根。

items.en: The -i- between the two parts is a Latin stem vowel, as in insectivore and frugivore; it is not a separate morpheme.
items.cn: 两部分之间的 -i- 是拉丁词干元音，如 insectivore、frugivore；它并不是独立的语素。

items.en: The term became standard in ecology in the twentieth century, when feeding roles were separated from taxonomic groups. The exact first use is not firmly established.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词在生态学中成为标准术语，当时取食角色开始与分类群分开讨论。确切首见出处尚无定论。

items.en: Stream and soil ecology adopted detritivore to describe shredders and soil animals, giving the word a practical field meaning.
items.cn: 溪流与土壤生态学采用 detritivore 描述撕碎者与土壤动物，使这个词获得了野外实践意义。

note.en: The first group shares the pieces; the second holds other feeding roles.
note.cn: 第一组共享构词成分；第二组是其他取食角色。

entries.definition: Describes the diet; detritivore is the animal itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述食性；detritivore 指动物本身。

entries.definition: The habit or process of eating detritus, not the eater.
entries.definitionCN: 指食碎屑的习性过程，不是取食者。

entries.definition: The dead fragments themselves; the animal is named after them.
entries.definitionCN: 指死亡碎片本身；动物以它们命名。

entries.definition: A microbe that mineralizes dead matter; a detritivore chews particles but leaves the chemistry to microbes.
entries.definitionCN: 把死亡物质矿化的微生物；食碎屑动物咀嚼颗粒，化学分解则留给微生物。

entries.definition: An animal feeding on dead bodies; detritivores take plant and particle fragments as well as animal remains.
entries.definitionCN: 以尸体为食的动物；食碎屑动物还取食植物与颗粒碎片。

entries.definition: An animal that feeds on living plants or algae; detritivores feed on what is already dead.
entries.definitionCN: 取食活植物或藻类的动物；食碎屑动物取食已经死去的材料。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the food word plus the eater ending.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：食物名词加取食者词尾。

normal.en: detritus + -vore: a detritus-eater, exactly parallel to insectivore.
normal.cn: detritus + -vore：食碎屑者，与 insectivore 构词完全平行。

normal.en: Typical examples are earthworms, woodlice, caddis larvae and amphipods.
normal.cn: 典型例子有蚯蚓、潮虫、石蛾幼虫与端足类。

normal.en: The phrase detritus food chain names the pathway that starts with dead matter.
normal.cn: detritus food chain 指以死亡物质为起点的食物链路径。

normal.en: The word draws the line against decomposer and scavenger.
normal.cn: 这个词与 decomposer、scavenger 划出了界限。

normal.en: The -i- is a stem vowel, not a separate piece of meaning.
normal.cn: -i- 是词干元音，并不是独立的意义单位。

abstract.en: Think of a kitchen where nobody cooks: the staff only reheat what yesterday left behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一间没人做饭的厨房：员工只把昨天剩下的东西重新加热。

abstract.en: A detritivore is a paper shredder that also eats the paper.
abstract.cn: 食碎屑动物就是一台把纸碎掉、还把纸吃掉的碎纸机。

abstract.en: In a stream, dead leaves are the harvest, and the shredders are the mill.
abstract.cn: 在溪流里，落叶是收成，撕碎者就是磨坊。

examples.en: Detritivores speed up decay by cutting large fragments into small ones.
examples.cn: 食碎屑动物把大碎片切成小碎片，从而加快腐烂。

examples.en: The pond's detritivores keep the bottom from sealing under uneaten feed.
examples.cn: 池塘里的食碎屑动物防止池底被剩余饲料封住。

examples.en: Trace fossils show that detritivores were active in the ancient sediment.
examples.cn: 遗迹化石表明食碎屑动物曾在古代沉积物中活动。

dict_mnemonic.text: detritus（碎屑）+ vore（吞食者）→ 吃碎屑的动物

root: 拉丁语 detritus「被磨掉的东西」（deterere 的过去分词，de- + terere「摩擦」）+ 拉丁语 vorare「吞食」+ -ore → detritivore「吞食碎屑者」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one relation: an animal and the dead fragments it eats. The setting may be a stream, soil, a feeding guild, a farm pond or a fossil bed.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保持同一个关系：动物与它取食的死亡碎片。场景可以是溪流、土壤、取食功能群、养殖池塘或化石层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small animal turning dead fragments into its own body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小动物把死亡碎片转化为自己的身体。

branches.en: THE CORE: the diet defines the animal, and the setting decides whether it shreds, mixes or grazes fragments.
branches.cn: 核心：食性定义了动物，而环境决定它是在撕碎、混合还是刮食碎片。

branches.en: THE GUILD: ecology groups all detritus feeders together regardless of species.
branches.cn: 功能群：生态学把所有食碎屑者归为一组，不论物种。

branches.en: THE DIVISION OF LABOUR: animals fragment, microbes mineralize.
branches.cn: 分工：动物负责破碎，微生物负责矿化。

branches.en: THE NAMED USERS: field guides name typical groups, and aquaculture employs them as cleaners.
branches.cn: 具名使用者：野外手册列出典型类群，水产养殖则把它们雇为清道夫。

branches.en: THE PAST: trace fossils let paleontologists infer the same role in ancient sediments.
branches.cn: 过去：遗迹化石让古生物学家在古代沉积物中推断出同样的角色。

intro.en: Detritivore is a compound of a Latin participle-noun and a Latin eating root.
intro.cn: detritivore 由拉丁语分词名词与拉丁语「吃」的词根复合而成。

latinIntro.en: The pieces are detritus 'rubbed-away material' and vorare 'to devour'; the linking -i- is a stem vowel.
latinIntro.cn: 成分是 detritus「被磨掉的材料」与 vorare「吞食」；连接元音 -i- 是词干元音。

items.example: The detritivore hides under the leaf mat.
items.exampleCN: 这种食碎屑动物藏在叶垫下面。

items.example: The detritivorous shrimp grazes the bottom.
items.exampleCN: 这种食碎屑的虾在底部觅食。

items.example: Detritivory dominates in headwater streams.
items.exampleCN: 食碎屑在溪流源头占主导。

items.example: Detritus collects behind the fallen branch.
items.exampleCN: 碎屑积聚在倒下的树枝后面。

items.example: Detrital food webs begin with dead matter.
items.exampleCN: 碎屑食物网以死亡物质为起点。

items.example: Herbivore and detritivore differ in what is alive.
items.exampleCN: 食草者与食碎屑者的区别在于食物是否还活着。

items.example: Carnivore is the third classic feeding type.
items.exampleCN: 食肉者是第三种经典的食性类型。

items.example: Voracious and detritivore share the eating root.
items.exampleCN: voracious 与 detritivore 共享「吃」的词根。

definition_en: the role and position a species occupies in an ecosystem, including its habitat, food and interactions
core_image: 同一片树林里，每种鸟各占一层枝叶、各吃一类虫子
scene: Each warbler occupies a different ecological niche, feeding at a different height in the canopy.
sceneCN: 这里 ecological niche 是「生态位」（第 1 个义项：物种在群落中的功能位置）；句意：每种林莺占据不同的生态位，在树冠的不同高度取食。

pos.zh: 生态位；生态小生境（可数，复数 ecological niches）

forms.label: 形容词
forms.form: niche（生态位的；小众的，作定语）

derivatives.zh: 生态位；合适的位置；小众市场

senses.title: A species' role in a community
senses.definition: the functional position of a species in an ecosystem, including what it eats and what eats it
senses.definitionCN: 物种在生态系统中的功能位置，包括它吃什么以及被谁吃
senses.example: The owl's ecological niche keeps rodent numbers in check.
senses.exampleCN: 猫头鹰的生态位控制着啮齿动物的数量。
senses.why: Ecology borrowed niche, a word for a recess or comfortable spot, and turned it into the place a species fills in a network of interactions.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用了 niche 这个表示「凹处、合适位置」的词，把它变成物种在相互作用网络中所填补的位置。

senses.title: The physical microhabitat
senses.definition: the specific physical space and conditions a species occupies, such as a crevice or a canopy layer
senses.definitionCN: 物种占据的具体物理空间与条件，如岩缝或某一树冠层
senses.example: The lichen's ecological niche is a narrow band of shaded bark.
senses.exampleCN: 这种地衣的生态位是一条狭窄的遮阴树皮带。
senses.why: The original architectural sense of niche as a recess survives here: the species lives in a particular pocket of the environment.
senses.whyCN: niche 原本的建筑义「壁龛」在此保留：物种生活在环境中的某个特定凹处。

senses.title: The niche it could fill
senses.definition: the full range of conditions and resources a species could use without competitors
senses.definitionCN: 在没有竞争者时，物种理论上可利用的全部条件与资源范围
senses.example: The fundamental ecological niche of the plant includes wet soils it never reaches.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物的基础生态位包含它从未到达的湿润土壤。
senses.why: Modeling separates what a species can use from what it does use, and the adjective fundamental marks the theoretical maximum.
senses.whyCN: 建模把「物种能用什么」与「实际用了什么」分开，fundamental 标记的是理论上的最大值。

senses.title: The niche it actually holds
senses.definition: the narrower range a species actually occupies when competitors and enemies are present
senses.definitionCN: 在竞争者和天敌存在时，物种实际占据的较窄范围
senses.example: Competition shrinks the realized ecological niche to a few metres of shoreline.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争把实际生态位压缩到几米长的岸线。
senses.why: Realized marks the difference between potential and outcome, a central distinction in niche theory.
senses.whyCN: realized 标记「潜力」与「结果」之间的差异，这是生态位理论的核心区分。

senses.title: The splitting of niches
senses.definition: the process by which species diverge in resource use so that they can coexist
senses.definitionCN: 物种在资源利用上分化从而得以共存的过程
senses.example: Niche differentiation let five finch species share one island.
senses.exampleCN: 生态位分化使五种雀类共享一座岛。
senses.why: When species overlap too much, one excludes the other; divergence in the niche is how coexistence becomes possible.
senses.whyCN: 当物种重叠过多时，一方会排除另一方；生态位分化正是共存成为可能的途径。

senses.title: The niche an organism builds
senses.definition: the modification of the environment by an organism, which changes the selective pressures on itself and others
senses.definitionCN: 生物改造环境，从而改变自身与其他生物所受选择压力的过程
senses.example: Beaver dams are a clear case of ecological niche construction.
senses.exampleCN: 河狸坝是生态位构建的明显例子。
senses.why: Niche construction reverses the usual arrow: instead of occupying a pre-existing slot, the organism reshapes the slot itself.
senses.whyCN: 生态位构建反转了通常的箭头：生物不是占据一个既有的格子，而是重塑这个格子本身。

senses.title: A gap in a market
senses.definition: in business, a small specialised segment of a market that is not served by larger competitors
senses.definitionCN: 商业中未被大型竞争者覆盖的细分市场
senses.example: The brand found an ecological niche among buyers of repair tools.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌在维修工具购买者中找到了一个市场空隙。
senses.why: Business borrows the ecological image of a position that is open because others cannot use it.
senses.whyCN: 商业借用了生态学意象：某个位置之所以空着，是因为其他参与者无法利用它。

senses.title: A person's fitting place
senses.titleCN: 个人或组织的合适位置
senses.definition: figuratively, a role or position in an organisation that suits a particular person or group
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指组织中适合某个个人或群体的角色与位置
senses.example: She carved out an ecological niche as the team's translator between engineers and clients.
senses.exampleCN: 她在工程师与客户之间担任翻译，为自己开辟出一个合适的位置。
senses.why: The metaphor generalises the idea of a slot that fits and is not already taken by someone else.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻把「合适且尚未被他人占据的格子」这一想法普遍化。

intro.en: Ecological niche joins a Greek-derived science word to a French architectural word whose deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: ecological niche 把一个源自希腊语的科学词，接在一个源自法语的建筑词上，而后者更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Ecology was coined in 1866 by Ernst Haeckel from Greek oikos, 'house, dwelling', and -logia, 'study of'. The image is the household of nature.
items.cn: ecology 由恩斯特·海克尔于 1866 年用希腊语 oikos「房屋、住所」与 -logia「研究」造出，其意象是「自然之家」。

items.en: Niche comes from French niche, a recess in a wall, from Italian nicchia. Italian nicchio may mean 'shell', but the step from shell to recess is not securely documented.
items.cn: niche 来自法语 niche「墙上的凹处」，再上溯意大利语 nicchia。意大利语 nicchio 可能意为「贝壳」，但从「贝壳」到「凹处」这一步缺乏可靠文献支持。

items.en: The deeper origin of nicchia is disputed. Some link it to Latin mitulus 'mussel', others to a different Mediterranean source; no single etymology is accepted as certain.
items.cn: nicchia 的更早来源存在争议。有人把它联系到拉丁语 mitulus「贻贝」，也有人指向其他地中海来源；没有一种词源被公认为确凿。

items.en: In the early twentieth century, ecologists used niche for the place of a species in a community. The exact date and author of the transfer are debated.
items.cn: 20 世纪初，生态学家用 niche 指物种在群落中的位置。这一转移的确切年代与提出者仍有争论。

items.en: Mid-twentieth-century work by G. Evelyn Hutchinson formalized the niche as a multidimensional space of conditions and resources, producing the fundamental and realized distinction.
items.cn: 20 世纪中叶 G. 伊夫林·哈钦森的工作把生态位形式化为条件与资源构成的多维空间，并由此产生基础生态位与实际生态位的区分。

items.en: Late twentieth-century marketing extended niche to specialised market segments, and ordinary speech extended it to any comfortable role.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期的营销把 niche 扩展到细分市场，日常语言则把它扩展到任何「合适的位置」。

note.en: The first group is easily confused with niche itself; the second holds related ecological positions.
note.cn: 第一组容易与 niche 本身混淆；第二组是相关的生态位置概念。

entries.definition: The same concept without the modifier; in marketing it means a specialised segment.
entries.definitionCN: 去掉修饰语的同一概念；在营销中指细分市场。

entries.definition: The physical place where an organism lives; the niche is its role and resource use there.
entries.definitionCN: 指生物生活的物理场所；生态位指它在那里扮演的角色与资源利用方式。

entries.definition: The community plus its physical environment; a niche is one position inside that whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指群落及其物理环境；生态位是这一整体内部的一个位置。

entries.definition: The full theoretical range without competitors; the realized niche is the part actually held.
entries.definitionCN: 无竞争者的完整理论范围；实际生态位是其中真正占据的部分。

entries.definition: The narrower range left after competition and predation; it is always a subset of the fundamental niche.
entries.definitionCN: 竞争与捕食之后留下的较窄范围；始终是基础生态位的子集。

entries.definition: The splitting of resources among species so that each uses a different part; the outcome of niche differentiation.
entries.definitionCN: 物种间把资源分开，各自使用不同部分；是生态位分化的结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the architectural image and the standard ecological pairs.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：建筑意象与标准的生态学配对。

normal.en: A niche is a recess in a wall; an ecological niche is a recess in the living community.
normal.cn: niche 是墙上的凹处；ecological niche 是生命群落中的凹处。

normal.en: The standard pair is fundamental versus realized niche.
normal.cn: 标准配对是基础生态位与实际生态位。

normal.en: Niche differentiation explains coexistence; niche construction explains environmental change.
normal.cn: 生态位分化解释共存；生态位构建解释环境改变。

normal.en: Habitat is the address; niche is the job.
normal.cn: 栖息地是地址，生态位是职业。

normal.en: In marketing, the same word means a specialised gap competitors ignore.
normal.cn: 在营销中，同一个词指竞争者忽略的细分空隙。

abstract.en: Picture a theatre with many roles and one stage: each species auditions for a different part.
abstract.cn: 想象一座有许多角色、只有一个舞台的剧院：每个物种都在试演不同的角色。

abstract.en: A niche is not an empty chair but a job description written by the ecosystem.
abstract.cn: 生态位不是一把空椅子，而是生态系统写好的岗位说明。

abstract.en: A beaver does not find a niche; it renovates one.
abstract.cn: 河狸不是找到一个生态位，而是把它翻修改造。

examples.en: Two species cannot occupy the same ecological niche indefinitely.
examples.cn: 两个物种无法无限期地占据同一个生态位。

examples.en: The realized ecological niche of the frog shrank after a fish was introduced.
examples.cn: 引入一种鱼之后，这种青蛙的实际生态位缩小了。

examples.en: The startup survived by serving an ecological niche the giants ignored.
examples.cn: 这家初创企业靠服务巨头忽视的细分空隙而存活。

dict_mnemonic.text: ecological（生态的）+ niche（壁龛）→ 生态系统里的「壁龛」→ 生态位

root: ecological 来自希腊语 oikos「房屋、住所」+ -logia「研究」（ecology 由海克尔 1866 年造出）；niche 来自法语 niche「墙上的凹处」，再上溯意大利语 nicchia，其更早来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a position that a species, a product or a person can occupy: the role, the microhabitat, the potential and actual ranges, the split, the built niche, the market gap and the personal fit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述一个可被占据的位置：角色、小生境、潜在与实际范围、分化、被构建的生态位、市场空隙与个人适配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slot in a living community, shaped by what the occupant does there.
core.cn: 核心意象：生命群落中的一个格子，由占据者在那里的作为塑形。

branches.en: THE CORE: the architectural recess becomes both a functional role and a physical pocket.
branches.cn: 核心：建筑的凹处同时变成功能角色与物理小空间。

branches.en: THE TWO RANGES: theory distinguishes what could be used from what is actually held.
branches.cn: 两种范围：理论区分「本可使用」与「实际占据」。

branches.en: THE SPLIT: differentiation allows several species to share one community.
branches.cn: 分化：生态位分化让多个物种共享一个群落。

branches.en: THE BUILD: an organism can remodel the slot instead of merely filling it.
branches.cn: 构建：生物可以改造这个格子，而不只是填充它。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: business and everyday speech reuse the idea of an open, fitting position.
branches.cn: 隐喻：商业与日常语言复用「空缺而合适的位置」这一想法。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek-derived adjective of ecology to a French noun of architecture.
intro.cn: 这个短语把源自希腊语的生态学形容词接在法语建筑名词上。

latinIntro.en: Ecology is Greek oikos plus -logia, Latinized in form. Niche is French, ultimately perhaps from Latin mitulus, but that step is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: ecology 是希腊语 oikos 加 -logia，形式上被拉丁化。niche 来自法语，最终也许源于拉丁语 mitulus，但这一步并不确定。

items.example: The two beetles divide the ecological niche by height.
items.exampleCN: 这两种甲虫按高度划分生态位。

items.example: The statue stands in a niche above the door.
items.exampleCN: 雕像立在门上方的壁龛中。

items.meaning: the study of the household of nature
items.example: Ecology studies how organisms share resources.
items.exampleCN: 生态学研究生物如何共享资源。

items.meaning: the place where an organism lives
items.example: Habitat is the address; niche is the role.
items.exampleCN: 栖息地是地址，生态位是角色。

items.example: Each niche belongs to a larger ecosystem.
items.exampleCN: 每个生态位都属于更大的生态系统。

items.example: Niche differentiation reduced competition.
items.exampleCN: 生态位分化减少了竞争。

items.example: Niche construction changes the rules for later generations.
items.exampleCN: 生态位构建改变后代面对的条件。

items.example: The firm chose a niche market rather than the mass market.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司选择细分市场而不是大众市场。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb form, third person singular of habitare

definition_en: the reduction or disappearance of the natural places where species live
core_image: 推土机推过一片林地，鸟群在空中盘旋却无处落下
scene: Logging caused habitat loss across most of the valley within a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 habitat loss 是「栖息地丧失」（第 1 个义项：物种自然栖息地的减少或消失）；句意：伐木在十年之内造成山谷大部分地区的栖息地丧失。

pos.zh: 栖息地丧失；生境丧失（不可数，指过程或状态）

collocations.zh: 栖息地丧失的驱动因素
农业造成的栖息地丧失

forms.label: 不可数用法
forms.form: habitat loss（指过程或总体状况时不可数）

forms.label: 复数（指多起损失事件）
forms.form: habitat losses（多起栖息地丧失事件，较少用）

senses.title: The disappearance of living space
senses.definition: the reduction or complete disappearance of the natural environment a species needs
senses.definitionCN: 物种所需自然环境的减少或完全消失
senses.example: Habitat loss is the leading threat to amphibians worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 栖息地丧失是全球两栖动物的首要威胁。
senses.why: The phrase names a state and a process at once: the place is lost, and the losing is ongoing.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语同时命名状态与过程：场所已经失去，而失去仍在持续。

senses.title: A shrinking area
senses.definition: a decline in the total area of a particular habitat type
senses.definitionCN: 某一类栖息地总面积的下降
senses.example: Satellite images measured habitat loss in the wetland over thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星影像测量了这片湿地三十年间栖息地面积的减少。
senses.why: Remote sensing quantifies loss as area, turning the phrase into a measurable variable.
senses.whyCN: 遥感把丧失量化为面积，使这个说法成为一个可测量的变量。

senses.title: Loss through degradation
senses.definition: the effective loss of habitat quality even where the area remains
senses.definitionCN: 面积虽在、栖息地质量却实际丧失的情况
senses.example: Pollution caused habitat loss without removing a single hectare.
senses.exampleCN: 污染造成栖息地丧失，却没有减少一公顷面积。
senses.why: Conservation practice treats unusable habitat as lost, so quality counts as well as area.
senses.whyCN: 保护实践把无法使用的栖息地也算作丧失，因此质量与面积同等重要。

senses.title: Loss through land conversion
senses.definition: the conversion of natural land to farms, roads, mines or cities
senses.definitionCN: 把自然土地转为农田、道路、矿场或城市
senses.example: The road project accounted for most of the habitat loss in the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 道路工程是该走廊栖息地丧失的主要原因。
senses.why: This sense focuses on the human action that removes habitat, the commonest cause in policy documents.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项聚焦于移除栖息地的人类行为，也是政策文件中最常见的成因表述。

senses.title: A conservation threat
senses.titleCN: 保护生物学中的威胁因子
senses.definition: in conservation biology, one of the main pressures ranked against species survival
senses.definitionCN: 保护生物学中按物种存续风险排序的主要压力之一
senses.example: The assessment listed habitat loss ahead of hunting and climate change.
senses.exampleCN: 这项评估把栖息地丧失排在捕猎与气候变化之前。
senses.why: Threat ranking needs a stable label, so the phrase became a standard category in red lists.
senses.whyCN: 威胁排序需要一个稳定的标签，因此这个说法成为红色名录中的标准类别。

senses.title: A driver of extinction
senses.definition: a process that raises extinction risk by removing the places species depend on
senses.definitionCN: 通过移除物种依赖的场所而提高灭绝风险的过程
senses.example: Habitat loss drove the island's endemic birds to the edge of extinction.
senses.exampleCN: 栖息地丧失把这岛上的特有鸟类推向灭绝边缘。
senses.why: The phrase connects a local change to a global outcome, which is why it dominates extinction analysis.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法把局部变化与全球结果连接起来，因此它在灭绝分析中占主导地位。

senses.title: A policy and legal category
senses.definition: in law and planning, the loss of habitat that must be avoided, mitigated or compensated
senses.definitionCN: 法律与规划中必须避免、减缓或补偿的栖息地损失
senses.example: The developer paid for habitat loss compensation on an adjacent site.
senses.exampleCN: 开发商为邻近场地的栖息地丧失支付了补偿。
senses.why: Regulation turns the ecological fact into an obligation, and the phrase names the item to be balanced.
senses.whyCN: 监管把生态事实变成义务，这个说法命名的是需要被平衡的项目。

senses.title: Loss of a familiar setting
senses.definition: figuratively, the disappearance of the conditions in which a group or activity once thrived
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指某群体或活动曾赖以繁荣的条件消失
senses.example: Small bookshops faced habitat loss as the high street changed.
senses.exampleCN: 随着商业街变迁，小书店面临「栖息地丧失」的处境。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the ecological structure: a way of life needs a place, and the place is going away.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻保留了生态结构：一种生活方式需要场所，而场所正在消失。

intro.en: Habitat loss is a modern compound of a Latin verb form and an Old English noun.
intro.cn: habitat loss 是现代复合词，由拉丁语动词形式与古英语名词构成。

items.en: Habitat is the third-person singular present of Latin habitare, 'to dwell', itself frequentative of habere, 'to have, hold'. It appears in Latin texts as 'it dwells here'.
items.cn: habitat 是拉丁语 habitare「居住」的第三人称单数现在时，而 habitare 又是 habere「拥有、持有」的反复形式。它在拉丁语文本中意为「它住在这里」。

items.en: English naturalists adopted habitat in the eighteenth century for the place where a species lives, probably through translations of Latin botanical descriptions.
items.cn: 英语博物学家在 18 世纪采用 habitat 指物种生活的地方，大概是通过拉丁植物描述的翻译而来。

items.en: Loss comes from Old English los, 'destruction, loss', related to the verb leosan, 'to lose'. It is native Germanic, not Latin.
items.cn: loss 来自古英语 los「毁坏、丧失」，与动词 leosan「失去」相关，属本族日耳曼语，而非拉丁语。

items.en: Habitat loss became a standard phrase with twentieth-century conservation biology, as habitat destruction was identified as the main cause of species decline. The exact first use is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 随着 20 世纪保护生物学的发展，habitat loss 成为标准说法，因为栖息地破坏被认定是物种衰退的主要原因。确切首见年代尚无定论。

items.en: Late twentieth-century environmental law and planning adopted the phrase for impacts to be avoided, mitigated or offset.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期的环境法与规划采用这一说法，指必须避免、减缓或抵消的影响。

note.en: The first group is easily confused with the phrase; the second holds related conservation terms.
note.cn: 第一组容易与这个短语混淆；第二组是相关保护术语。

entries.definition: A decline in habitat quality while the area remains; habitat loss usually implies area is gone.
entries.definitionCN: 面积仍在而质量下降；habitat loss 通常意味着面积已经消失。

entries.definition: The division of habitat into isolated patches; the total area may be similar, but connectivity is lost.
entries.definitionCN: 栖息地被切成孤立斑块；总面积可能相近，但连通性丧失。

entries.definition: The physical removal of habitat; habitat loss is the resulting reduction, which can also come from degradation.
entries.definitionCN: 对栖息地的物理清除；habitat loss 是由此导致的减少，也可由退化引起。

entries.definition: The clearing of forest, a major cause of habitat loss but not the whole category.
entries.definitionCN: 砍伐森林，是栖息地丧失的主要原因之一，但不等于整个类别。

entries.definition: Changing natural land to another use; it is the usual mechanism behind habitat loss.
entries.definitionCN: 把自然土地改为其他用途；是栖息地丧失背后的常见机制。

entries.definition: The decline of species and genetic variety; habitat loss is one of its main drivers.
entries.definitionCN: 物种与遗传多样性的下降；栖息地丧失是其主因之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin 'it dwells' and the standard conservation pairings.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语「它居住」与标准保护搭配。

normal.en: habitat is literally 'it dwells'; habitat loss is the dwelling going away.
normal.cn: habitat 字面就是「它居住」；habitat loss 就是住所消失。

normal.en: The standard pair is habitat loss and fragmentation.
normal.cn: 标准配对是栖息地丧失与破碎化。

normal.en: Area, quality and connectivity give the three related terms: loss, degradation, fragmentation.
normal.cn: 面积、质量与连通性对应三个相关术语：丧失、退化、破碎化。

normal.en: Policy phrases include driver of habitat loss and habitat loss compensation.
normal.cn: 政策搭配包括栖息地丧失的驱动因素与栖息地丧失补偿。

normal.en: The bulldozer at the forest edge is the word's plainest image.
normal.cn: 林缘的推土机，是这个词最朴素的画面。

abstract.en: Think of a theatre losing its stage: the actors remain, but there is nowhere to perform.
abstract.cn: 想象一座剧院失去舞台：演员还在，却没有地方演出。

abstract.en: A species without habitat is a key without a lock.
abstract.cn: 没有栖息地的物种，就是一把没有锁的钥匙。

abstract.en: In business, habitat loss means the street changed before the shop did.
abstract.cn: 在商业里，栖息地丧失意味着街道变了，而店铺还没变。

examples.en: Agriculture is the largest single cause of habitat loss worldwide.
examples.cn: 农业是全球栖息地丧失最大的单一原因。

examples.en: The reserve was created to slow habitat loss along the river.
examples.cn: 设立保护区是为了减缓沿河的栖息地丧失。

examples.en: The report links habitat loss to the decline of migratory birds.
examples.cn: 报告把栖息地丧失与候鸟数量下降联系起来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a needed place disappearing: as a state, an area, a quality, a land-use change, a ranked threat, an extinction driver, a legal item and a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述「所需场所消失」：作为状态、面积、质量、土地转用、排序威胁、灭绝驱动、法律项目与隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a place that life needs, taken away.
core.cn: 核心意象：生命所需的场所被拿走。

branches.en: THE CORE: the place is gone, and the loss can be measured as area.
branches.cn: 核心：场所消失，而丧失可以用面积来测量。

branches.en: THE MECHANISMS: quality can fall without area shrinking, and land can be converted to other uses.
branches.cn: 机制：面积不缩小时质量也会下降，土地也可被转为其他用途。

branches.en: THE CONSEQUENCE: conservation ranks the pressure, and extinction analysis names it as a driver.
branches.cn: 后果：保护学对它排序，灭绝分析把它列为驱动因素。

branches.en: THE RULE: law turns the loss into something to avoid, mitigate or compensate.
branches.cn: 规则：法律把这种丧失变成需要避免、减缓或补偿的事项。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any way of life can lose the conditions that supported it.
branches.cn: 隐喻：任何生活方式都可能失去支撑它的条件。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Latin-derived noun of dwelling with a native Germanic noun of losing.
intro.cn: 这个短语把源自拉丁语的「居住」名词与本族日耳曼语的「失去」名词组合起来。

latinIntro.en: Habitat is Latin habitare 'to dwell', from habere 'to have'; loss is Old English los, with no Latin element.
latinIntro.cn: habitat 是拉丁语 habitare「居住」，源自 habere「拥有」；loss 是古英语 los，不含拉丁语成分。

items.exampleCN: 栖息地丧失威胁着这片滨海沼泽。

items.example: Habitat restoration can reverse part of the loss.

items.example: Deforestation is a common cause of habitat loss.
items.exampleCN: 毁林是栖息地丧失的常见原因。

definition_zh: 栖息地破碎化；生境破碎化
definition_en: the division of a continuous habitat into smaller, isolated patches
core_image: 一整片森林被道路和农田切成一块块孤岛
scene: The new highway accelerated habitat fragmentation, isolating the forest into small patches.
sceneCN: 这里 habitat fragmentation 是「栖息地破碎化」（第 1 个义项：连续栖息地被分割成孤立斑块的过程）；句意：新高速公路加速了栖息地破碎化，把森林分割成小片孤岛。

collocations.zh: 狭义的栖息地破碎化（仅指斑块配置变化）

senses.title: The splitting of continuous habitat
senses.definition: the process by which a large continuous habitat is divided into smaller pieces
senses.definitionCN: 大片连续栖息地被分割成更小片块的过程
senses.example: Road building is a common cause of habitat fragmentation.
senses.exampleCN: 道路建设是栖息地破碎化的常见原因。
senses.why: The word fragment carries the image of breaking a whole into pieces, and the ecological phrase applies it to living space.
senses.whyCN: fragment 一词带有「把整体打碎」的形象，这个生态短语把它用在生存空间上。

senses.title: The patchwork result
senses.definition: the state of a landscape once it consists of isolated habitat patches
senses.definitionCN: 景观已由孤立栖息地斑块组成时的状态
senses.example: The map shows severe fragmentation after two decades of clearing.
senses.exampleCN: 地图显示，经过二十年的开垦，破碎化已很严重。
senses.why: The same noun names both process and outcome, as with many ecological terms describing landscape change.
senses.whyCN: 与许多描述景观变化的生态术语一样，这个名词同时指过程与结果。

senses.title: Loss of connectivity
senses.definition: the reduction of movement routes between patches for plants and animals
senses.definitionCN: 动植物在斑块之间移动路线减少
senses.example: Fragmentation cut the corridor that once linked the two valleys.
senses.exampleCN: 破碎化切断了过去连接两座山谷的走廊。
senses.why: Patch isolation matters because organisms need to move; fragmentation is measured partly by how hard that movement becomes.
senses.whyCN: 斑块隔离之所以重要，是因为生物需要移动；破碎化在一定程度上以移动的困难程度来衡量。

senses.title: More edge, less interior
senses.definition: the increase of edge habitat at the expense of deep interior habitat
senses.definitionCN: 边缘生境增加、深层内部生境减少
senses.example: Fragmentation brought more edge, where nest predators thrive.
senses.exampleCN: 破碎化带来更多边缘地带，而巢捕食者在那里更易繁衍。
senses.why: Small patches have proportionally more edge, so fragmentation changes the conditions inside the remaining habitat.
senses.whyCN: 小斑块的边缘比例更高，因此破碎化改变了剩余栖息地内部的条件。

senses.title: Distinguished from habitat loss
senses.definition: the change in habitat configuration that can occur even when total area stays the same
senses.definitionCN: 总面积不变时仍可能发生的栖息地配置变化
senses.example: The study separated fragmentation from loss by holding total forest area constant.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究在保持森林总面积不变的情况下，把破碎化与丧失区分开来。
senses.why: Conservation science needs the distinction because area and arrangement affect species differently.
senses.whyCN: 保护科学需要这一区分，因为面积与布局对物种的影响不同。

senses.title: A landscape-scale process
senses.definition: in landscape ecology, the change in the number, size and arrangement of habitat patches
senses.definitionCN: 景观生态学中斑块数量、大小与布局的变化
senses.example: Fragmentation is analysed at the scale of whole landscapes, not single fields.
senses.exampleCN: 破碎化要在整个景观的尺度上分析，而不是单块田地。
senses.why: Landscape ecology measures composition and configuration, and fragmentation is the configuration variable.
senses.whyCN: 景观生态学测量组成与配置，而破碎化就是配置变量。

senses.title: Genetic consequences
senses.definition: the loss of genetic diversity and gene flow when populations become isolated in small patches
senses.definitionCN: 种群在小斑块中孤立后，遗传多样性与基因流丧失
senses.example: Fragmentation left the lizards with almost no gene flow between ridges.
senses.exampleCN: 破碎化使这些蜥蜴在山脊之间几乎没有基因流。
senses.why: Isolation reduces mating options, so the landscape pattern becomes a genetic process over time.
senses.whyCN: 隔离减少了交配选择，因此景观格局随时间变成遗传过程。

senses.title: A metaphor for division
senses.definition: figuratively, the splitting of an organisation, field or community into disconnected parts
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指组织、领域或社群被切成互不连接的部分
senses.example: Critics warned of habitat fragmentation inside the university's research groups.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者警告这所大学的研究团队内部正在出现「栖息地破碎化」。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the spatial structure: what was one connected whole becomes isolated fragments.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻保留了空间结构：原本连通的一个整体变成孤立的碎片。

intro.en: Habitat fragmentation pairs a Latin noun of dwelling with a Latin noun of breaking.
intro.cn: habitat fragmentation 把一个拉丁语「居住」名词与一个拉丁语「破碎」名词组合起来。

items.en: Habitat is the third-person singular of habitare, 'to dwell', from habere, 'to have, hold'. English naturalists adopted it in the eighteenth century for a species' living place.
items.cn: habitat 是 habitare「居住」的第三人称单数，源自 habere「拥有、持有」。英语博物学家在 18 世纪采用它指物种的生活场所。

items.en: Fragment comes from Latin fragmentum, 'a piece broken off', from frangere, 'to break'. The same verb underlies fracture and fragile.
items.cn: fragment 来自拉丁语 fragmentum「打下来的碎片」，源自 frangere「打破」。同一个动词也是 fracture 与 fragile 的来源。

items.en: Fragmentation entered English in the nineteenth century as a general noun for breaking into pieces, used in geology and medicine before ecology.
items.cn: fragmentation 在 19 世纪作为「裂成碎片」的通用名词进入英语，先用于地质学与医学，后用于生态学。

items.en: Mid-twentieth-century landscape ecology gave the phrase its technical sense, distinguishing the number and arrangement of patches from total habitat area. The exact first use is not firmly established.
items.cn: 20 世纪中叶的景观生态学赋予这个短语技术含义，把斑块的数量与布局同栖息地总面积区分开来。确切首见出处尚无定论。

items.en: Late twentieth-century conservation planning adopted fragmentation as a standard impact to assess alongside habitat loss.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期的保护规划把破碎化作为与栖息地丧失并列评估的标准影响。

note.en: The first group is easily confused with the phrase; the second holds related landscape terms.
note.cn: 第一组容易与这个短语混淆；第二组是相关景观术语。

entries.definition: The reduction of total habitat area; fragmentation changes arrangement and can occur without area loss.
entries.definitionCN: 指栖息地总面积的减少；破碎化改变布局，可在面积不变时发生。

entries.definition: A fall in habitat quality, such as pollution or invasive species; fragmentation is about spatial pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 栖息地质量下降，如污染或入侵物种；破碎化关乎空间格局。

entries.definition: The general process of breaking into fragments, usable for data, rocks or societies; the habitat phrase narrows it.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指裂成碎片的过程，可用于数据、岩石或社会；加上 habitat 后范围收窄。

entries.definition: The separation of populations or patches; fragmentation is the spatial process that produces isolation.
entries.definitionCN: 种群或斑块被分隔；破碎化是产生隔离的空间过程。

entries.definition: The changed conditions at a habitat boundary; small fragments have more edge, so the effect grows.
entries.definitionCN: 栖息地边界处条件的改变；小碎片边缘更多，因此效应增强。

entries.definition: The quality of occurring in patches; fragmentation is the human-driven change that increases patchiness.
entries.definitionCN: 以斑块形式分布的性质；破碎化是人类驱动、使斑块化加剧的变化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the breaking root and the area-versus-arrangement distinction.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「打破」的词根，以及面积与布局的区分。

normal.en: fragment comes from frangere 'to break'; the same root gives fracture and fragile.
normal.cn: fragment 来自 frangere「打破」，同根词有 fracture 与 fragile。

normal.en: The key contrast is habitat loss (area) versus fragmentation (arrangement).
normal.cn: 关键对比是栖息地丧失（面积）与破碎化（布局）。

normal.en: The automatic consequences are isolation, edge effect and reduced gene flow.
normal.cn: 自动带来的后果是隔离、边缘效应与基因流减少。

normal.en: Landscape ecology measures fragmentation as patch number, size and spacing.
normal.cn: 景观生态学用斑块数量、大小与间距来衡量破碎化。

normal.en: The forest cut by roads into islands is the standard picture.
normal.cn: 被道路切成岛屿的森林，是标准画面。

abstract.en: Think of a sheet of paper cut into pieces: the paper is all still there, but nothing can travel across it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸被剪成碎片：纸都还在，但没有任何东西能横穿整张纸。

abstract.en: A fragmented habitat is an archipelago on land.
abstract.cn: 破碎化的栖息地，就是陆地上的群岛。

abstract.en: In an organisation, fragmentation is when every team has its own island and no bridge.
abstract.cn: 在组织里，破碎化就是每个团队都有自己的岛，却没有桥。

examples.en: Habitat fragmentation makes it harder for animals to find mates.
examples.cn: 栖息地破碎化使动物更难找到配偶。

examples.en: The researchers measured fragmentation separately from habitat loss.
examples.cn: 研究者把破碎化与栖息地丧失分开测量。

examples.en: Restoring hedgerows can reduce the effects of habitat fragmentation.
examples.cn: 恢复树篱可以减轻栖息地破碎化的影响。

dict_mnemonic.text: habitat（栖息地）+ fragmentation（碎成片）→ 栖息地被切碎 → 栖息地破碎化

root: habitat 为拉丁语 habitare「居住」的第三人称单数（源自 habere「拥有」）；fragmentation 来自拉丁语 fragmentum「碎片」，源自 frangere「打破」，加名词后缀 -ation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one spatial change and its effects: the splitting process, the patchwork state, lost connectivity, edge growth, the contrast with loss, the landscape measure, genetic isolation and a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述同一种空间变化及其后果：分割过程、斑块状态、连通性丧失、边缘增加、与丧失的对比、景观度量、遗传隔离与隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one connected living space cut into islands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片连通的生存空间被切成岛屿。

branches.en: THE CORE: the process and its result share one noun, as a continuous habitat becomes patchwork.
branches.cn: 核心：过程与结果共用同一个名词，连续栖息地变成斑块拼图。

branches.en: THE MECHANISMS: movement routes disappear and edge conditions expand into the interior.
branches.cn: 机制：移动路线消失，边缘条件向内部扩张。

branches.en: THE MEASUREMENT: science separates arrangement from area and measures both at landscape scale.
branches.cn: 度量：科学把布局与面积分开，并在景观尺度上测量两者。

branches.en: THE GENETIC EFFECT: isolation becomes visible in reduced gene flow.
branches.cn: 遗传效应：隔离在基因流减少中变得可见。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any connected whole can be described as fragmented.
branches.cn: 隐喻：任何连通整体都可被描述为破碎化。

intro.en: The phrase joins a noun of dwelling to a noun of breaking.
intro.cn: 这个短语把「居住」名词与「破碎」名词组合起来。

latinIntro.en: Both Latin elements are clear: habitare 'to dwell' and frangere 'to break', the latter giving fragmentum and the English -ation noun.
latinIntro.cn: 两个拉丁语成分都清楚：habitare「居住」与 frangere「打破」，后者产生 fragmentum 以及英语的 -ation 名词。

items.example: Habitat fragmentation isolates the remaining population.
items.exampleCN: 栖息地破碎化使剩余种群孤立。

items.meaning: the process of breaking into pieces
items.example: Fragmentation increased after the road opened.
items.exampleCN: 道路开通后破碎化加剧。

items.example: A fragment of forest remains on the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 山脊上还剩一片森林碎片。

items.example: The fragmented landscape has few corridors.
items.exampleCN: 这片破碎的景观几乎没有走廊。

items.example: Fracture and fragment share the breaking root.
items.exampleCN: fracture 与 fragment 共享「打破」词根。

items.example: Fragile habitats suffer most from fragmentation.
items.exampleCN: 脆弱的栖息地受破碎化影响最大。

items.meaning: the degree to which patches are linked
items.example: Connectivity falls as fragmentation rises.
items.exampleCN: 破碎化上升时连通性下降。

items.meaning: a small area distinct from its surroundings
items.meaningCN: 与周围不同的小块区域
items.example: Each patch holds a separate population.
items.exampleCN: 每个斑块容纳一个独立种群。
